# Tool reference — AUTHOR surface

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-authoring-tool-reference.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

This page is generated directly from `authorFacingToolDefinitions`
(`packages/spellkave-tool-authoring/src/authoring.ts`) — the SAME TypeBox
parameter schemas a host binds to `createAuthorFacingTools` and hands to an
agent's tool-calling loop. Every name, required/optional flag, type, default,
and description below is the tool's own runtime schema, not hand-copied prose:
if a verb's parameters change, this page changes with it (the
`authoring-tool-reference-drift` skgate registry gate fails the build otherwise). Every tool below that declares an offline-executable
example also carries a real, EXECUTED "Example" call + result — never
hand-typed — run against a bespoke in-memory scratch workspace by this
generator; a tool whose `run` requires a live connection instead carries an
honest "requires an active connection" marker.
Corpus revision fields use `<packaged-corpus-revision>` here to avoid hashing a
page containing its own digest; actual docs responses carry the current digest.

For a narrative walkthrough of the calling PATTERN (which verbs to call in
what order, smart defaults, stage-then-commit), see
[`getting-started-with-verbs.md`](./getting-started-with-verbs.md). For the
underlying TOML row shapes these verbs write, see
[`manifest-format.md`](./manifest-format.md). For the PLAYER/DM tool surface —
a different audience, not served through `spellkave_docs` — see
[the PLAYER tool reference](../../spellkave-tool-player/docs/tool-reference.md).

## `spellkave_docs`

**Modding Docs** — execution mode `parallel`.

Orient on the packaged authoring corpus (DOCS-ONLY). Index (`shape: "index"`): id/title/kind/summary/has_example. Query (`shape: "hits"`): ranked summary+excerpt only (not full bodies). Doc (`shape: "doc"`): one id — oversized docs default to outline (headings); pass `section` for one heading or `full` for the entire body. Narrow hits with `doc_paths`; `limit` default 3. Reads ONLY the packaged corpus.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `doc` | no | string |  | Exact corpus id (a `rel` from the index or a hit, e.g. 'dm-oversight') — returns that ONE doc whole: its prose body, the worked-example walkthrough when the id has both halves, and the complete example manifest TOML when `has_example` is true. This is how you get something copyable rather than only readable. Mutually exclusive with `query`; takes precedence if both are set. |
| `doc_paths` | no | array<string> |  | Optional corpus-id filter (substring match) restricting the search to specific packaged docs. Only applies with `query` set; can only narrow the corpus, never widen it. |
| `full` | no | boolean |  | With `doc`, force the complete body even when oversized (tool-reference, long references). Prefer `section` instead. Default false. |
| `limit` | no | number |  | Max number of doc slices to return when `query` is set (default 3). |
| `outline` | no | boolean |  | With `doc`, return title + summary + heading list only (no full body). Default for oversized docs when neither `section` nor `full` is set. |
| `query` | no | string |  | Free-text question about how to author something, e.g. 'how do I express object decay over time'. Matched (keyword/heading) against the packaged authoring corpus. Omit to list the bounded corpus index instead of querying it. |
| `section` | no | string |  | Optional heading text or anchor within `doc` — returns only that section's markdown instead of the full body. Unknown section fails (does not silently return the whole doc). Ignored without `doc`. |

```json
{}
```

## `spellkave_query`

**Query Manifest / Definitions** — execution mode `parallel`.

Read the authored world — merges the former spellkave_manifest_inspect + spellkave_lookup, plus the definition-lookup gap's missing single-row detail/ref-traversal capability, into ONE tool. Dispatch is inferred from which fields you pass (no mode flag): omit `kind` for a workspace/target summary (bundle ids + row-kind -> count map); pass `kind` alone (or with `pattern`) for a bounded catalog list (default ids-only; add fields:'preferred' or fields:[col,…] to project extra scalars — e.g. entities preferred yields name+place_node_id for who-is-where in one call); pass `kind` + `id` for the complete authored row, its source, and (by default) its outbound/inbound refs — chase a ref by re-calling this tool with its own {kind, id} (e.g. a capability -> its affordance_templates -> their action_definitions -> outcome_templates). Sources, in order: the workspace scratch manifest, plus the active connection-level `target` when wired, or the legacy live `context.db` when no target is configured (result.source says which). Offline with neither, this is workspace-only. `target` overrides the source for THIS call only (read-only — write verbs offer no such override).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | Restrict to rows stamped with this bundle_id (summary/list shapes only). |
| `explore` | no | object |  | Bounded admitted discovery. Summary inventories all three collections with coverage and per-kind counts (incomplete kinds are lower bounds). Instance summary/search count objects once by default; view rows preserves technical rows and explicit kind selects rows. Defaults to live; search collection follows kind, otherwise unrestricted text searches all collections and empty text defaults to places. An explicit collection must agree with kind. Explicit workspace/local source is never unioned. Follow exact returned references; no read grants write permission. |
| `fields` | no | "preferred" \\| array<string> |  | List shape only (`kind` without `id`; ignored for detail/summary/schema). Default (omit): token-safe catalog — each item is only `{ id, bundle_id? }`. `preferred`: project a small kind-specific field set (e.g. entities → name, place_node_id, kind, entity_def_id) so one list call can answer who-is-where without N detail round-trips. Explicit string[]: project exactly those column names from each row (unknown/missing names omitted; nested values skipped). `id` is always present; `bundle_id` is included when the row has it. |
| `id` | no | string |  | An exact natural-key value within `kind` — returns the complete authored row (detail shape), its source, and (by default) its refs. For a composite-keyed `*_tag` satellite kind, this is its ordered key fields' values joined by '::' (e.g. 'srd/wis::ability_score' for resource_definition_tag's `{resource_definition_id, tag}` — get the exact ids from a `kind`-only list call first). Mutually exclusive with `pattern`; requires `kind`. |
| `kind` | no | string |  | A manifest row-kind name (a ROW_KIND_NATURAL_KEY key — e.g. 'capability_definitions', 'affordance_templates', 'action_definitions', 'outcome_templates', 'entity_definitions', 'area_shape_definitions', 'resource_definitions'), the SAME vocabulary spellkave_write_rows and every define_* verb already use — not a closed enum. Also accepts a `*_tag` satellite kind (e.g. 'resource_definition_tag', 'capability_definition_tag') — these have a TWO-field composite key (parent id + tag) instead of a single natural key; see `schema: true` for the field order. Omit for a workspace/target summary (bundle ids + a row-kind -> count map) instead of listing one kind. |
| `pattern` | no | string |  | A substring filter on `kind`'s ids (its natural-key value, or its '::'-joined composite-key value for a `*_tag` satellite kind) — returns a filtered list instead of the full catalog. Mutually exclusive with `id`; requires `kind`. |
| `refs` | no | "none" \\| "outbound" \\| "both" |  | Detail shape only (`kind`+`id`; ignored otherwise). 'outbound': fields on this row pointing elsewhere (already-computed string-ref heuristic). 'both' additionally computes inbound_refs — every OTHER row anywhere in the resolved source whose own outbound ref points AT this row, grouped by referencing kind — so a caller traverses a chain (e.g. capability -> affordance -> action -> outcome) by re-calling spellkave_query with a ref's own {kind, id}, no separate traversal tool needed. Default: 'both' when `id` is set. |
| `schema` | no | boolean |  | Ask what a row of `kind` may CONTAIN instead of which rows exist : with `kind`, that row kind's required fields, field types, and natural/composite key; without `kind`, the row-kind vocabulary itself (every kind the manifest schema defines, flagged for whether this tool can also list its rows). Schema covers all 79 manifest row kinds — a superset of the ~53 `id`/`pattern` can address: the 40 with a single-column natural key, plus the `*_tag` satellite kinds and `tag_capability_grant` with a two-field composite key (finding ; sk-bwd). Ignores `id`/`pattern`/`bundle`/`target`: a row kind's shape is the same everywhere, so no source is consulted. |
| `target` | no | "workspace" \\| "local" \\| "live" |  | connection-level target override (READ-only — no write verb offers this): 'workspace' reads ONLY the workspace scratch manifest, ignoring any connection-level target/live db this call would otherwise consult. 'local' reads ONLY the active local folder target — errors if none is configured. 'live' reads ONLY the active live target (or the legacy live db when no target is wired at all) — errors if neither is available. Omit for the default union: workspace + whatever is configured (result.source says which). |

#### `explore`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  |  |
| `collection` | no | "places" \\| "definitions" \\| "instances" |  |  |
| `cursor` | no | string |  |  |
| `direction` | no | "outbound" \\| "inbound" |  |  |
| `facets` | no | boolean |  | Summary only: include definition counts by kind and detailed authored tag facets. Default false; the compact summary offers this as a follow-up. |
| `field` | no | string |  |  |
| `fields` | no | array<string> |  | search/detail only: scalar names from the collection schema for search, or the selected row kind's schema for detail; `label` is also selectable. |
| `kind` | no | string |  |  |
| `limit` | no | integer |  | Page size. Default 12 tag facets for summary, 5 for search (ranked: label equals, starts with, contains, then other text), 20 otherwise. |
| `offset` | no | integer |  |  |
| `operation` | yes | "summary" \\| "search" \\| "detail" \\| "neighbors" \\| "references" \\| "field" |  |  |
| `ref` | no | object |  |  |
| `source` | no | "live" \\| "workspace" \\| "local" |  |  |
| `source_id` | no | string |  | The `source.source_id` of the response that returned `ref`/`within`. Required with `ref` and `within`; another source, world or connection is refused. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | Summary: count these literal tags separately on definitions and distinct objects. Search: require all tags. Tags are never inherited from definitions. |
| `text` | no | string |  |  |
| `view` | no | "objects" \\| "rows" |  | Summary/search/neighbors only. Default objects: instance bodies once, without tag rows. Explicit kind selects rows. Use rows for the technical inventory. |
| `within` | no | object |  |  |

##### `explore.ref`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  |  |
| `id` | yes | string |  |  |
| `kind` | yes | string |  |  |

##### `explore.within`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  |  |
| `id` | yes | string |  |  |
| `kind` | yes | string |  |  |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "kind": "resource_definitions",
  "id": "aoe_blast/hp"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "shape": "detail",
  "kind": "resource_definitions",
  "id": "aoe_blast/hp",
  "found": true,
  "source": "workspace",
  "row": {
    "resource_definition_id": "aoe_blast/hp",
    "bundle_id": "aoe_blast",
    "display_name": "Hit Points",
    "value_kind": "int",
    "min_value": 0,
    "max_value": 30,
    "recovery_rule": "long_rest",
    "initial_value": 30
  },
  "outbound_refs": [],
  "inbound_refs": []
}
```

## `spellkave_eval`

**Evaluate DSL Expression** — execution mode `parallel`.

Evaluate a Spellkave DSL expression offline using the wasm-compiled resolution evaluator. Accepts expression source, kind (predicate, int, or text), author-supplied facts grouped by subject or pool, and die faces in draw order. Returns the result value with its type, draws used, and evaluation trace, or a named rejection naming the cause.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `dice` | no | array<integer> |  | Die faces in draw order consumed by stochastic roll operators and roll tables. |
| `expression` | yes | string |  | DSL source text to evaluate offline. |
| `facts` | no | object |  | The values the expression reads, grouped by subject (actor, target, location, session, world, actor.wielded_item, equipped items, bindings, event), plus roll_tables, item_sources, roll_modifier_bias, event_kind, occupants_at, peers_near_target, channel_pools. Validated strictly in Rust. |
| `kind` | yes | "predicate" \\| "int" \\| "text" |  | Expression result kind: 'predicate', 'int', or 'text'. |

## `spellkave_map_graph`

**Map Graph** — execution mode `parallel`.

Render the authored place-graph as the shared spatial-graph view. Sources rows only through the same workspace/target/live resolution as spellkave_query (place_graphs, place_nodes, place_edges, actor_spatial_locations). output_type picks the ONE artifact computed and returned: 'svg' (default) — this tool's picture-first interactive use case: the raw SVG in details.svg plus an ImageContent PNG for hosts that render tool images (Pi TUI / Ghostty Kitty). 'utf8'/'ascii'/'braille' return that text variant in the like-named details field instead (no image). 'inventory' skips the graph picture entirely, details.inventory only. 'jpg' writes a backdrop-composed JPEG to output_dir/output_name and returns its path as details.jpg_path — no svg/ascii/utf8/braille text in the response.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `graph` | no | string |  | Optional place_graph_id filter — when set, draw that graph (any substrate). Omit to compose every outdoor positioned graph (world map). |
| `lod` | no | "structure" \\| "furnished" |  | structure = rooms/routes only (no occupancy badges); furnished = + actor counts (default). |
| `output_dir` | no | string |  | output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Directory to write the map-art JPEG into — absolute, or RELATIVE to the host process's own cwd. Optional: omit for a fresh temp directory (mkdtemp). Resolves this graph's authored [[map_layers]] backdrop (unmasked — same drawn-in-full contract every backdrop render in this package follows), rasterizes via resvg then encodes via ffmpeg -q:v 4, skipping the rewrite when an unchanged render already sits there (deterministic churn guard). |
| `output_name` | no | string |  | output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Base filename (no extension) for the JPEG written under output_dir. Optional: omit for a name derived from graph, or 'map' when graph itself is also omitted (a world-compose call). |
| `output_type` | no | "utf8" \\| "ascii" \\| "braille" \\| "inventory" \\| "svg" \\| "jpg" |  | Which single artifact to render — the engine computes ONLY this one (bead sk-due: the old `terminal` param picked the text body while the engine rendered svg + utf8 + ascii + braille + inventory regardless, every call). 'svg' (default) — this tool's own interactive picture-first use case: the raw SVG in details.svg plus an ImageContent PNG for hosts that render tool images (Pi TUI / Ghostty Kitty). 'utf8'/'ascii'/'braille' return that text variant in the like-named details field instead (no image). 'inventory' skips the graph picture entirely, details.inventory only. 'jpg' writes a backdrop-composed JPEG to output_dir/output_name and returns its path as details.jpg_path — no svg/ascii/utf8/braille text in the response. |
| `slice` | no | "elevation_band" \\| "all_floors_offset" \\| "topology_only" \\| "metric" \\| "h3_world" |  | How to project multi-floor / unpositioned graphs: elevation_band (one floor), all_floors_offset (floors side-by-side), topology_only (adjacency layout), metric (all z in one plane), h3_world (outdoor multi-graph from cell_res10 — same plane idea as web WorldMapView). Omit for auto (indoor multi-z → elevation_band at z=0; outdoor compose uses h3 when cells present). |
| `target` | no | "workspace" \\| "local" \\| "live" |  | Same read-only source override as spellkave_query (`workspace` \| `local` \| `live`). Omit for the default workspace+configured-target union. |
| `z` | no | number |  | Elevation for slice=elevation_band (default 0). Matches pose_elevation. |
| `z_tolerance` | no | number |  | Half-width of elevation_band in elevation units (default 0.5). |

### Example

_Requires an active connection — no offline example; this tool cannot be demonstrated without a live/local target wired._

## `spellkave_declare_inexpressible`

**Declare Inexpressible** — execution mode `sequential`.

Declare that no documented row kind / DSL form can express this intent within the validator's surface — a runtime/schema gap surfaced through authoring. A well-justified 'I cannot express this' is a SUCCESSFUL finding, not a failure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `reason` | yes | string |  | Precisely why no documented row kind / DSL form can express this intent within the validator's surface. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "reason": "No documented row kind expresses a resource pool that regenerates on a delay after combat ends — every recovery_rule is a fixed enum (e.g. long_rest/short_rest), not a scheduled predicate."
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "reason": "No documented row kind expresses a resource pool that regenerates on a delay after combat ends — every recovery_rule is a fixed enum (e.g. long_rest/short_rest), not a scheduled predicate."
}
```

## `spellkave_note_doc_gap`

**Note Doc Gap** — execution mode `sequential`.

Record a discrepancy between what the modding docs implied and what the validator actually accepted. Does NOT end your run — keep authoring. Sharpens the docs shipped to other authors.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `actual` | yes | string |  | What the validator actually did — the discrepancy. |
| `doc` | yes | string |  | Which corpus doc id you were working from, e.g. 'dsl-grammar'. |
| `expected` | yes | string |  | What the doc led you to expect. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "doc": "manifest-format",
  "expected": "resource_definitions.recovery_rule accepts an arbitrary string.",
  "actual": "The validator rejects any recovery_rule outside the documented closed set."
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "doc": "manifest-format",
  "expected": "resource_definitions.recovery_rule accepts an arbitrary string.",
  "actual": "The validator rejects any recovery_rule outside the documented closed set."
}
```

## `spellkave_author_place`

**Author Place (verb PoC)** — execution mode `sequential`.

PoC : author ONE place_graph + its place_nodes (+ optional place_edges) in a single call, wrapping the existing patchManifest place ops. Self-scaffolds the `[[bundles]]` header if `bundle` has none yet (FIX②b). Nodes get metric positions (explicit x/y or auto circle/line) and optional elevation. substrate defaults to outdoor; pass substrate:'indoor' for buildings. PoC boundary: one place_graph per call. map_graph draws outdoor world-compose by default; pass graph=<id> to draw an indoor plan. Top-level `description` sets the GRAPH's own description; each `nodes[].description` sets that ONE node's own arrival prose instead (T5 follow-up) — author both when a node deserves its own sensory detail beyond the graph-level blurb.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bearing` | no | number |  | Clockwise rotation degrees relative to parent/world frame (ADR-0029). Default 0. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | Sets the generated place_graph's own `description` column (— a first-class, never load-bearing authoring field, not a metadata_attachments row). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | place_graph display_name; default title-cased graph local id. |
| `edges` | yes | array<array<string>> |  | [from_node_id, to_node_id] pairs; both ends must be in `nodes`. Pass [] for disconnected nodes (e.g. two same-radius cells with no traversal edge between them, as the worked example does). |
| `metres_per_unit` | no | number |  | Graph unit → metres (ADR-0029). Default 1. Outdoor world maps often use >1. |
| `nodes` | yes | array<object> |  | One or more place nodes. Every id must share ONE common parent path (one place_graph per call — a PoC boundary); the FIRST node becomes the place_graph's anchor_node_id. |
| `origin_cell_res10` | no | string |  | Root outdoor H3 res10 anchor as decimal u64 string. Only composition roots should set this; res7/res4 parents are derived. Nested graphs omit (origin stays 0). |
| `parent_graph_id` | no | string |  | Composition parent place_graph_id (ADR-0029 / Item 25). Empty/omit = root. Nested outdoor graphs project into the parent frame on the world map. |
| `substrate` | no | string |  | substrate_id for the graph and every node (core: outdoor \| indoor \| tactical). Default 'outdoor'. Houses/interiors should use 'indoor'. |

#### `nodes[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `cell_res10` | no | string |  | Optional outdoor H3 res10 cell as decimal u64 string (parents res7/res4 derived via h3-js). Prefer strings so values above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER stay exact. |
| `description` | no | string |  | Sets THIS node's own `place_nodes.description` column (T5 follow-up, pattern: a first-class field, never a metadata_attachments detour — same shape as the top-level `description` param below, which sets the GRAPH's own description instead). Read by movement-observation tools (e.g. spellkave_move) as the arrival prose for THIS node; falls back to the graph's own description only on a graph-crossing move when omitted. |
| `elevation` | no | number |  | Optional graph-local pose_elevation (metres-ish via graph metres_per_unit). Use for floors/cellars (e.g. 0 ground, -3 cellar). Omit for 0 with pose_elevation_present=true. |
| `extent_params_json` | no | string |  | place_nodes.extent_params_json — the params_json paired with `extent_shape_id` (e.g. '{"radius_m": 2.5}' for core/area/sphere). Only meaningful alongside `extent_shape_id`. |
| `extent_shape_id` | no | string |  | place_nodes.extent_shape_id (place-node-extent D-2, sk-71u): an explicit spatial extent for THIS node — one of the KNOWN_AREA_SHAPE_IDS kernel shapes (e.g. 'core/area/sphere', 'core/area/cube'). Overrides the bundle's own default_extent_shape_id (spellkave_define_bundle) for this node only. Pair with `extent_params_json`; omit both to fall back to the bundle default. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Fully-qualified place-node id '<place_graph_id>/<local_id>' (e.g. 'aoe_blast/arena/center'). PoC boundary: bare local ids are not supported. |
| `name` | no | string |  | display_name; defaults to a title-cased local id. |
| `x` | no | number |  | Optional metric graph-local pos_x (integer graph units). When any node omits x/y, author_place auto-layouts all nodes on a circle (n>=3) or a line (n=1..2). |
| `y` | no | number |  | Optional metric graph-local pos_y (integer graph units). See `x`. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "aoe_blast/arena/center",
      "name": "Arena Center"
    },
    {
      "id": "aoe_blast/arena/fringe",
      "name": "Arena Fringe"
    }
  ],
  "edges": [],
  "description": "Blast arena: center holds the caster + targets, fringe proves the radius-0 boundary."
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 4,
  "diagnostics": [],
  "place_graph_id": "aoe_blast/arena",
  "layout": [
    "aoe_blast/arena/center \"Arena Center\" @ (0, 0, z=0)",
    "aoe_blast/arena/fringe \"Arena Fringe\" @ (10, 0, z=0)"
  ],
  "edges": []
}
```

## `spellkave_link_places`

**Link Places** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author a portal between two existing place_nodes (same graph or cross-graph). Writes place_edges with place_graph_id "" when graphs differ (Stonehill pattern), sets substrate_crossing automatically for outdoor↔indoor. Does NOT attach a place_edge_affordance by default (ADR-0101): an ordinary edge just inherits the bundle/graph movement_default (spellkave_set_movement_default) via place_edges.inherit_movement_default, which defaults to true — zero per-edge rows for ordinary walking. Pass portal:true (+ affordance_template_id / bindings_json) only for a special affordance you want attached to THIS edge at creation time; spellkave_bind_edge_affordance is the preferred (FK-validated) path for that, including after the edge already exists. Use after spellkave_author_place on both sides.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `affordance_template_id` | no | string |  | place_edge_affordance.affordance_template_id when portal is true (portal defaults to false — see that field). Default "core/affordance/traverse_open_portal" when portal is true and this is omitted. Self-sufficient packs pass e.g. "srd/affordance/step". |
| `bidirectional` | no | boolean |  | Author reverse edge too (default true). |
| `bindings_json` | no | string |  | place_edge_affordance.bindings_json when portal is true (default ""). e.g. '{"movement_reach_resource":"srd/speed-walk","long_running_move_session":"srd/long_running_move"}' for srd Step. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on generated edges. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle`. |
| `cell_anchor` | no | string |  | H3 res10 cell anchor as decimal u64 string for substrate_crossing edges (MF-VAL-102). Omit to use dummy 1 (legacy); outdoor portals should pass a real cell. |
| `description` | no | string |  | Optional edge description. |
| `door` | no | boolean |  | If true, attach metadata namespace place.door on each edge_key (inert; locks later). |
| `from` | yes | string |  | Fully-qualified place_node id (must already exist in workspace/target). |
| `portal` | no | boolean |  | Attach a place_edge_affordance on each edge (default FALSE, ADR-0101 — ordinary edges inherit the bundle/graph movement_default instead, no per-edge row needed). Pass true only to attach a special affordance right at creation time; template defaults to core/affordance/traverse_open_portal unless affordance_template_id is set. |
| `substrate_crossing` | no | boolean |  | Force substrate_crossing. Omit to auto: true when the two nodes' substrates differ, or when they belong to different place_graphs (cross-graph portal). |
| `to` | yes | string |  | Fully-qualified place_node id (must already exist in workspace/target). |

## `spellkave_bind_edge_affordance`

**Bind Edge Affordance** — execution mode `sequential`.

Attach a place_edge_affordance to an edge that ALREADY exists (author it first via spellkave_link_places / spellkave_author_place) — closes the write_rows-only gap where a raw place_edge_affordance write validated nothing against edge_key (sk-9ll.2). Derives edge_key(s) exactly as spellkave_link_places does (from->to), validates the edge AND the affordance_template_id both already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target), then upserts by (edge_key, affordance_template_id, mode_id) — re-authoring the SAME triple REPLACES bindings_json rather than duplicating (mirrors the Rust add-place-edge-affordance patch op; ADR-0101 widened the key with mode_id). Optionally also REPLACES the edge's own inherit_movement_default flag (requires the edge already authored in THIS workspace).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `affordance_template_id` | yes | string |  | place_edge_affordance.affordance_template_id — must already resolve to an authored affordance_templates row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not auto-create it. |
| `bidirectional` | no | boolean |  | Attach to both from->to and to->from edges (default true) — mirrors spellkave_link_places' own default. Both edges must already exist when true. Pass false to bind only the from->to direction. |
| `bindings_json` | no | string |  | place_edge_affordance.bindings_json (default ""). e.g. '{"movement_reach_resource":"srd/speed-walk"}' for srd Step. |
| `from` | yes | string |  | place_edges.from_node_id of an edge that ALREADY exists (workspace, live, or the active target) — this call never creates one. Author it first via spellkave_link_places / spellkave_author_place. |
| `inherit_movement_default` | no | boolean |  | place_edges.inherit_movement_default (ADR-0101 D-1, schema default true) — REPLACES the flag on every already-existing edge this call targets (from->to, and to->from too when bidirectional). false means the edge owns its FULL mode set from its own place_edge_affordance rows alone (the fly-only-chasm idiom); true (or omitting this param) leaves/restores the resolved bundle/graph movement_default in play. Requires the edge to already be an authored [[place_edges]] row IN THIS WORKSPACE (not just live/target) — this is a whole-row re-author under the hood, so it needs the edge's other columns already in hand to avoid silently dropping them. |
| `mode_id` | no | string |  | place_edge_affordance.mode_id (ADR-0101 D-1, default "" — the implicit default mode). An open author-chosen id (e.g. "fly", "swim") — rows sharing one (edge_key, mode_id) AND-join (all must pass); distinct mode_ids on the SAME edge OR (the cheapest passing mode charges and supplies the long-running-move session). Upserts by (edge_key, affordance_template_id, mode_id) — the SAME template under two different mode_ids on one edge is a sibling row, not a replace. |
| `to` | yes | string |  | place_edges.to_node_id of the same already-existing edge. |

## `spellkave_set_movement_default`

**Set Movement Default** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author a bundle- or graph-scoped default traversal mode (ADR-0101) — the primitive that makes ordinary walking need ZERO per-edge place_edge_affordance rows (A-1). Validates affordance_template_id (and place_graph_id, when given) both already resolve, then upserts by (bundle_id, place_graph_id, mode_id, affordance_template_id) — re-authoring the SAME scope+mode+template REPLACES bindings_json; a second template in the same scope+mode is a sibling row (AND-join); a distinct mode_id is a third alternative (OR, cheapest-mode charges).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `affordance_template_id` | yes | string |  | movement_defaults.affordance_template_id — must already resolve to an authored affordance_templates row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not auto-create it. |
| `bindings_json` | no | string |  | movement_defaults.bindings_json (default ""). e.g. '{"movement_reach_resource":"srd/speed-walk","long_running_move_session":"srd/long_running_move"}' for srd Step. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | movement_defaults.bundle_id. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle`. ALWAYS the scope owner, even when place_graph_id narrows the row to one graph. |
| `mode_id` | no | string |  | movement_defaults.mode_id (default "" — the implicit default mode, same open author-chosen vocabulary as spellkave_bind_edge_affordance's mode_id, e.g. "fly"). Rows sharing one (scope, mode_id) AND-join; a distinct mode_id under the same scope is an alternative the kernel OR-picks the cheapest passing one from. |
| `place_graph_id` | no | string |  | movement_defaults.place_graph_id (default "" — bundle scope, applies to every edge in the bundle with no closer graph default). Set to scope this default to ONE place_graph instead (must already exist in workspace/live/target) — a graph-scoped default beats a bundle-scoped one for edges in that graph (D-2: edge > graph > bundle). |

### Example

_Requires an active connection — no offline example; this tool cannot be demonstrated without a live/local target wired._

## `spellkave_define_resource`

**Define Resource (verb PoC)** — execution mode `sequential`.

PoC (FIX②): author ONE resource_definitions row (a spell-slot/HP/charge-style pool) + its resource_definition_tag satellites (verb-UX round 2) in a single call — the scaffolding step placement-tool `resources` seeds and spellkave_define_behavior's `effect.write.resource`/`cost.pool` both need to already resolve against (neither verb fabricates bounds for a pool it didn't create). Self-scaffolds the `[[bundles]]` header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + EVERY tag satellite wholesale (fewer tags on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | Sets the generated resource_definitions row's own `description` column . |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | resource_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local resource stem; the full resource_definition_id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='aoe_blast', id='hp' -> 'aoe_blast/hp'). |
| `initial_value` | no | number |  | resource_definitions.initial_value — the object_state seed for an un-instantiated pool. Omit to fall back to min_value at runtime (a charges/gold-shaped pool); set e.g. to max_value for an HP-shaped pool that must start full. |
| `max_value` | yes | number |  | resource_definitions.max_value. |
| `min_value` | yes | number |  | resource_definitions.min_value. |
| `recovery_rule` | no | "none" \\| "persistent" \\| "long_rest" \\| "short_rest_partial_long_rest_full" |  | resource_definitions.recovery_rule (default 'none'). Closed PoC enum over the corpus's own observed vocabulary — the field itself is open-string at the schema level (ADR-0018). |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One resource_definition_tag row per tag (verb-UX round 2 — mirrors spellkave_define_entity_type/_condition/_niche's own `tags` fold instead of a separate spellkave_write_rows call). |
| `value_kind` | no | string |  | resource_definitions.value_kind (default 'int' — the only value observed corpus-wide). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "hp",
  "display_name": "Hit Points",
  "min_value": 0,
  "max_value": 30,
  "recovery_rule": "long_rest",
  "initial_value": 30
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 1,
  "diagnostics": [],
  "resource_definition_id": "aoe_blast/hp"
}
```

## `spellkave_place_entity`

**Place entity** — execution mode `sequential`.

Declaratively place authored world instances at build time. Emits an entity (+ optional object_state) without actor rows; use it for authored instances that are not steerable actors. Place them all at ONE node with the flat `at`/`count`/`resources`/`tags`, or split them across MULTIPLE nodes in the SAME call with `placements`; the two shapes are mutually exclusive. Self-scaffolds the `[[bundles]]` header if `bundle` has none yet (FIX②b). `kind` is explicit; optional `entity_def` is a separate fully-qualified catalog reference. Resolves `entity_def`/every `at` against the workspace, the active connection-level `target` when wired , and (legacy) live world when `context.db` is set directly — fails loudly on a dangling ref rather than authoring a broken instance. Returns the generated `entity_keys` (in placement order) for a later spellkave_define_behavior `grant_to`. workspace idempotency: pass `key_prefix` (flat shape) / `placements[].key_prefix` (placements shape) to give a placement an EXPLICIT, reproducible identity — a re-run with the SAME key_prefix upserts its owned rows. Anonymous placements are ADDITIVE — every call adds genuinely NEW instances, named '<bundle>/<short entity_def slug>_<n>' by default (falling back to the fully-qualified slug only on a short-slug collision across different entity_defs, addendum); name placements for idempotent scripts. sk-9ll.6: pass `entity_key` (flat) / `placements[].entity_key` (placements shape) instead of `key_prefix` for an explicit, LITERAL key with NO ordinal minted at all (e.g. a fixture-mandated 'bundle/hero') — mutually exclusive with `key_prefix`, only legal for a single instance. sk-9ll.7: pass `tags` (flat) / `placements[].tags` (placements shape) for INSTANCE-level `entity_tag` rows seeded on every instance in that shape — clear-and-reseed idempotent exactly like `resources` (a re-run with FEWER tags drops the stale ones). Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) is enforced by the shared validator at commit, not re-validated here; when a tag carries an authored tag_capability_grant, the result's `tag_capability_grants` reports the capability it live-grants (informational, never blocking). sk-ntz.1: pass `name` (flat) / `placements[].name` (placements shape) for a VERBATIM `entities.name`/`actors.name` override (no ordinal suffix appended) instead of the default title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` naming — the per-placement value wins when both flat `name` and a placement's own `name` are set. Pass `quantity` (flat) / `placements[].quantity` (placements shape) for an explicit `entities.quantity` (stack size) override instead of the schema default (1) — spellkave_place_entity ONLY; spellkave_place_actor rejects a set `quantity` outright (actors carry no stack) — the per-placement value wins here too. This authors manifest rows; runtime creation belongs to future DM spawn tools.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `at` | no | string |  | FLAT single-location shape: an already-authored place_node id every instance is placed at. Mutually exclusive with `placements` (FIX①) — set `at` (+ `count`/`resources`) for ONE location, or `placements` to split a batch across MULTIPLE locations in one call, never both. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `count` | no | number |  | FLAT shape only: how many identical instances to place (default 1). |
| `description` | no | string |  | Sets EVERY placed entity's own `description` column (across every placement) — e.g. 'the guard with the limp' (— a first-class, never load-bearing authoring field, not a metadata_attachments row). |
| `entity_def` | no | string |  | Optional fully-qualified catalog entity_def_id (contains '/', e.g. 'srd/monster/goblin') that must already resolve in the workspace or live world. `kind` remains explicit and independent. |
| `entity_key` | no | string |  | FLAT shape only (mutually exclusive with `placements` — set `placements[].entity_key` there instead). sk-9ll.6: see `placements[].entity_key`'s description for the full semantics — this is the same field, for the single-location flat shape. |
| `key_prefix` | no | string |  | FLAT shape only (mutually exclusive with `placements` — set `placements[].key_prefix` there instead). workspace idempotency: see `placements[].key_prefix`'s description for the full semantics — this is the same field, for the single-location flat shape. Mutually exclusive with `entity_key`. |
| `kind` | yes | "player" \\| "npc" \\| "item" \\| "place" |  | Manifest entity kind accepted by the current authoritative schema. The placement tool controls whether actor steering rows exist; `kind` does not. The open-vocabulary migration is tracked by. |
| `name` | no | string |  | sk-ntz.1: FLAT shape (also `placements[].name`, which wins when both are set): sets EVERY placed entity's own `entities.name`/`actors.name` verbatim (no ordinal suffix), instead of the default title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` naming. A first-class, never load-bearing authoring field, mirrors `description`'s own shared-across-every-placement convention. Mutually exclusive with `name_prefix`. Omit for the existing default — unchanged. |
| `name_prefix` | no | string |  | sk-jay0.7.15.3: FLAT shape (also `placements[].name_prefix`, which wins when both are set): replaces only the title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` half of the derived name and KEEPS the ordinal (`'<name_prefix> <n>'`) across every placed instance. The group-placement counterpart to verbatim `name`. Mutually exclusive with `name`. Illegal with `entity_key`. Omit for the existing default — unchanged. |
| `placements` | no | array<object> |  | MULTI-LOCATION shape (FIX①): one or more {at, count?, resources?, tags?} groups placing the SAME kind/entity_def split across DIFFERENT place_nodes in a single call (e.g. 3 targets at the blast center + 1 bystander at the fringe). Mutually exclusive with the flat `at`/`count`/`resources`/`tags` — set ONE shape or the other, never both. |
| `quantity` | no | integer |  | sk-ntz.1: FLAT shape (also `placements[].quantity`, which wins when both are set): sets EVERY placed entity's own `entities.quantity` (stack size) — spellkave_place_entity ONLY; spellkave_place_actor rejects a set `quantity` (actors carry no stack — use spellkave_place_entity for a stackable item instance instead). Omit for the schema default (1) — unchanged. |
| `resources` | no | array<object> |  | FLAT shape only: per-instance object_state overrides seeded on EVERY placed entity in this call (e.g. a non-default starting pool value). Does NOT declare the resource_definitions row itself (use spellkave_define_resource first). |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One INSTANCE-level entity_tag row per tag ('this goblin is the leader / faction X') — NOT an entity_definition_tag. Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) and dedup are enforced by the shared validator at commit; an unknown-grammar tag is reported as a diagnostic, not persisted. When a tag has authored tag_capability_grant rows (workspace/live), the result surfaces 'tag X grants capability Y' so the author sees the consequence — informational, never blocking. |

#### `placements[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `at` | yes | string |  | An already-authored place_node id (e.g. from spellkave_author_place) every instance in THIS placement is placed at. |
| `count` | no | number |  | How many identical instances at this placement (default 1). |
| `entity_key` | no | string |  | sk-9ll.6: THIS placement's own explicit, LITERAL entity_key, used verbatim — NO bundle prefix and NO ordinal suffix minted (contrast `key_prefix`'s derived '<bundle>/<key_prefix>_<n>'). For a pre-known exact key a script/fixture depends on (e.g. 'fastlane/hero') that does not follow the '<bundle>/<stem>_<n>' convention — the escape hatch that let raw write_rows chains mint exact keys this verb previously could not reproduce. Re-running with the SAME entity_key upserts its owned rows, same as `key_prefix`. Mutually exclusive with `key_prefix`; only legal for a single instance — omit `count` or set it to 1. |
| `key_prefix` | no | string |  | workspace idempotency: THIS placement's own explicit identity stem — keys become '<bundle>/<key_prefix>_<n>' (n restarts at 1 for this placement's own prefix, EVERY call — never derived from what already exists in the workspace). A re-run with the SAME key_prefix therefore reproduces the SAME keys and UPSERTS the rows owned by the selected placement tool. Omit for an anonymous, additive placement (default '<bundle>/<slugified entity_def>_<n>', numbered onward from whatever already exists in the workspace so repeated calls never collide) — name placements for idempotent scripts. Mutually exclusive with `entity_key`. |
| `name` | no | string |  | sk-ntz.1: THIS placement's own explicit, VERBATIM `entities.name`/`actors.name` override — used AS-IS on every instance in THIS placement, no ordinal suffix appended (contrast the default title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` naming, which DOES append an ordinal for multi-instance placements). Overrides the flat `name` when both are set (THIS placement's own `name` wins) — the escape hatch that let raw write_rows chains author a custom display name this verb previously could not reproduce (the fold this verb was widened for, sk-ntz.1, otherwise had no way to keep a fixture's own 'Fast-lane Hero' style name). Mutually exclusive with `name_prefix`. Omit for the existing default: title-cased `kind`/`entity_def`, ordinal-suffixed for multi-instance placements — unchanged. |
| `name_prefix` | no | string |  | sk-jay0.7.15.3: THIS placement's own display-name STEM — replaces only the title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` half of the derived name and KEEPS the ordinal (`'<name_prefix> <n>'`). The group-placement counterpart to verbatim `name` (which is used AS-IS with no ordinal, so a count>1 batch would otherwise share one identical name). Overrides the flat `name_prefix` when both are set (THIS placement's own `name_prefix` wins). Mutually exclusive with `name`. Illegal with `entity_key` (no ordinal is minted — use `name` for a single literal key). Omit for the existing default — unchanged. |
| `quantity` | no | integer |  | sk-ntz.1: THIS placement's own explicit `entities.quantity` (stack size) override for every instance in THIS placement — spellkave_place_entity ONLY (a stackable item's own on-instance count, e.g. a 10-credit purse); spellkave_place_actor rejects a set `quantity` outright (actors carry no stack — use spellkave_place_entity instead). Overrides the flat `quantity` when both are set (THIS placement's own `quantity` wins). Omit for the schema default (1) — unchanged. |
| `resources` | no | array<object> |  | Per-instance object_state overrides seeded on EVERY instance in THIS placement. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One INSTANCE-level entity_tag row per tag ('this goblin is the leader / faction X') — NOT an entity_definition_tag. Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) and dedup are enforced by the shared validator at commit; an unknown-grammar tag is reported as a diagnostic, not persisted. When a tag has authored tag_capability_grant rows (workspace/live), the result surfaces 'tag X grants capability Y' so the author sees the consequence — informational, never blocking. |

##### `placements[].resources[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `resource` | yes | string |  | A resource_definition_id (or any object_state state_id). |
| `value` | yes | number |  | The per-instance value_int override. |

#### `resources[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `resource` | yes | string |  | A resource_definition_id (or any object_state state_id). |
| `value` | yes | number |  | The per-instance value_int override. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "kind": "item",
  "at": "aoe_blast/arena/center",
  "key_prefix": "lever",
  "description": "A fixed brass lever set into the arena wall."
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 1,
  "diagnostics": [],
  "entity_keys": [
    "aoe_blast/lever_1"
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_remove_entity`

**Remove Entity** — execution mode `sequential`.

Remove a placed entity and its dependent instance rows from the active local root file, and clean matching staged scratch rows so a later flush cannot recreate it. Requires a local target; live targets are refused. Root headers, definitions and unrelated rows remain. Include-owned rows and surviving containment/ownership references are refused with recovery guidance before writes. Reports removed row counts. Does not change the running world: use diff/apply with prune separately.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `entity_key` | yes | string |  | Exact authored key of the placed entity to remove from the local root and staged scratch, e.g. my_adventure/torch. This edits files only; preview and apply world pruning separately. |

### Example

_Requires an active connection — no offline example; this tool cannot be demonstrated without a live/local target wired._

## `spellkave_place_actor`

**Place actor** — execution mode `sequential`.

Declaratively place authored world instances at build time. Emits an entity plus actor and actor_spatial_location rows; use it only for world participants that can be steered as actors. Place them all at ONE node with the flat `at`/`count`/`resources`/`tags`, or split them across MULTIPLE nodes in the SAME call with `placements`; the two shapes are mutually exclusive. Self-scaffolds the `[[bundles]]` header if `bundle` has none yet (FIX②b). `kind` is explicit; optional `entity_def` is a separate fully-qualified catalog reference. Resolves `entity_def`/every `at` against the workspace, the active connection-level `target` when wired , and (legacy) live world when `context.db` is set directly — fails loudly on a dangling ref rather than authoring a broken instance. Returns the generated `entity_keys` (in placement order) for a later spellkave_define_behavior `grant_to`. workspace idempotency: pass `key_prefix` (flat shape) / `placements[].key_prefix` (placements shape) to give a placement an EXPLICIT, reproducible identity — a re-run with the SAME key_prefix upserts its owned rows. Anonymous placements are ADDITIVE — every call adds genuinely NEW instances, named '<bundle>/<short entity_def slug>_<n>' by default (falling back to the fully-qualified slug only on a short-slug collision across different entity_defs, addendum); name placements for idempotent scripts. sk-9ll.6: pass `entity_key` (flat) / `placements[].entity_key` (placements shape) instead of `key_prefix` for an explicit, LITERAL key with NO ordinal minted at all (e.g. a fixture-mandated 'bundle/hero') — mutually exclusive with `key_prefix`, only legal for a single instance. sk-9ll.7: pass `tags` (flat) / `placements[].tags` (placements shape) for INSTANCE-level `entity_tag` rows seeded on every instance in that shape — clear-and-reseed idempotent exactly like `resources` (a re-run with FEWER tags drops the stale ones). Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) is enforced by the shared validator at commit, not re-validated here; when a tag carries an authored tag_capability_grant, the result's `tag_capability_grants` reports the capability it live-grants (informational, never blocking). sk-ntz.1: pass `name` (flat) / `placements[].name` (placements shape) for a VERBATIM `entities.name`/`actors.name` override (no ordinal suffix appended) instead of the default title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` naming — the per-placement value wins when both flat `name` and a placement's own `name` are set. Pass `quantity` (flat) / `placements[].quantity` (placements shape) for an explicit `entities.quantity` (stack size) override instead of the schema default (1) — spellkave_place_entity ONLY; spellkave_place_actor rejects a set `quantity` outright (actors carry no stack) — the per-placement value wins here too. This authors manifest rows; runtime creation belongs to future DM spawn tools.
