## `spellkave_bind_actor`

**Bind Actor (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

verb-UX round 6: bind an already-placed actor's identity (actor_identities, upsert-by-entity_key) and, optionally, grant it one or more capabilities (actor_capabilities) in a single call — folds the genesis-window self-grant idiom (an identity bind + a `frontier.apply_manifest` grant, the `srd/regdar`/`phandelver/hero` pattern every ad-hoc live-authored actor bundle needs post-core/player-retirement) from 2 spellkave_write_rows calls into 1. `entity_key` must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target) — place it first via spellkave_place_actor (mirrors spellkave_define_behavior's own `grant_to` precondition). workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME entity_key's identity bind REPLACES it (never duplicates — the server itself upserts on (actor_id, identity), and every corpus fixture binds one entity_key to exactly one identity); each capabilities[] grant upserts by (actor_entity_key, capability_id, source), mirroring add-capability-grant.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `capabilities` | no | array<object> |  | actor_capabilities grants issued to the SAME entity_key, alongside the identity bind. Default `[]` (identity-only bind — no grant). Ordinary capability rows are supported; frontier.* capability requests are refused with a pointer to spellkave_grant_role. |
| `entity_key` | yes | string |  | entity_key of an already-placed actor (e.g. via spellkave_place_actor) — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not place one. |
| `identity` | no | string |  | actor_identities.identity. Default '$sender' resolves to whoever submits the applying delta. Pass a concrete identity hex string only when binding to a KNOWN, fixed identity instead. |
| `role` | no | string |  | actor_identities.role. Default 'primary' (the corpus-dominant value; 'dm' is the one observed override). NOT a cosmetic label: r_claim_actor refuses every value but 'primary', so authoring 'dm' deliberately makes the seat un-self-claimable — right for a human DM anchor handed over by the operator, wrong for a programmatic seat that wants the self-claim path. It never affects visibility or write authority, which come from the capability grant alone. |

#### `capabilities[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `capability_id` | yes | string |  | actor_capabilities.capability_id — must already resolve to an authored capability_definitions row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not auto-create it. Privileged frontier.* ids use spellkave_grant_role with an explicit role and extent. |
| `extent_kind_ref` | no | string |  | actor_capabilities.extent_kind_ref. |
| `extent_ref` | no | string |  | actor_capabilities.extent_ref (ADR-0007 D-4 see-as scope). |
| `source` | no | string |  | actor_capabilities.source. Omit for the schema default 'manifest' (mirrors `add-capability-grant`'s own default). This is grant provenance, not authority over a role or extent. |
| `visibility` | no | string |  | actor_capabilities.visibility (ADR-0120 read-visibility override). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "entity_key": "aoe_blast/caster_1",
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "capability_id": "core/walk",
      "source": "core"
    }
  ]
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-365",
      "severity": "fatal",
      "message": "actor_capability 'aoe_blast/caster_1:core/walk' does not resolve in bundle 'aoe_blast' dependency closure or kernel bootstrap vocabulary",
      "path": "actor_capabilities.capability_id"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_tag_entity`

**Tag Entity (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

sk-ntz.2: retag an already-placed entity's INSTANCE-level entity_tag rows from a call/file OTHER than the one that placed it (e.g. crypt-fight.ts tagging a hero placed by hero.ts) — the narrow post-placement counterpart to spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own `tags` param, for exactly the case those verbs cannot cover: an entity_key placed elsewhere. `entity_key` must already carry an entities row (workspace or the active target) — place it first via spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor (mirrors spellkave_bind_actor's own precondition). Default `mode: 'add'` upserts the listed tags and leaves every OTHER tag on the entity untouched (idempotent); `mode: 'replace'` clears every existing entity_tag row for `entity_key` first, then reseeds exactly `tags` — use `replace` only when THIS call owns the entity's complete tag set, since it WOULD clobber tags authored by the entity's own placement call otherwise. Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) is enforced by the shared validator at commit, not re-validated here; when a tag carries an authored tag_capability_grant, the result's `tag_capability_grants` reports the capability it live-grants (informational, never blocking).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated entity_tag row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). NOTE: this is the bundle OWNING the new tag row(s), not necessarily the bundle that placed `entity_key` — a cross-bundle caller stamps ITS own bundle_id here (the kavemouth idiom this verb replaces: crypt-fight.ts/dm-npc.ts tag the hero placed in hero.ts, all three sharing one bundle in that fixture, but nothing requires it). |
| `entity_key` | yes | string |  | entity_key of an already-placed entity (e.g. via spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor, in THIS bundle or another) — must already carry an entities row (workspace or the active target); this call does not place one. Use this verb instead of re-invoking the placement tool when the entity's placement call lives in a DIFFERENT file/call than the one adding this tag. |
| `mode` | no | "add" \\| "replace" |  | Default 'add': upsert the listed tags, leaving every OTHER tag already on this entity_key untouched (idempotent — re-listing an already-present tag is a no-op) — the safe default for a cross-file caller that does not own the entity's full tag set (this verb's whole reason to exist: REPLACING would clobber tags the entity's OWN placement call already authored elsewhere). Set 'replace' only when THIS call owns the entity's complete tag set: it clears EVERY existing entity_tag row for `entity_key` first, then reseeds exactly `tags` (a re-run with fewer tags drops the stale ones, mirroring spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own clear-and-reseed). |
| `tags` | yes | array<string> |  | One INSTANCE-level entity_tag row per tag, mirroring spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own `tags` param exactly (same row shape, same MF-VAL-300 grammar, same tag_capability_grant diagnostic) — the difference is WHEN: this verb runs AFTER the entity already exists, against an entity_key placed by a DIFFERENT call/file. |

## `spellkave_equip_item`

**Equip Item (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

sk-9ll.3: equip an already-placed, already-stowed item into a named equipment slot on an actor (actor_equipment_slots, upsert-by-(actor_entity_key, slot_id)) — folds the 'give the hero a starter weapon' idiom's raw actor_equipment_slots write into one checked call. `slot_id` existence and `item_entity_key`'s existence/placeability are enforced by the SAME validator the linter and manifest admission use (no bespoke re-check here); THIS call's own precondition is the one thing only it can see across separate tool calls — a slot already occupied by a DIFFERENT item is a hard rejection (matches the runtime EquipItem affordance's SlotAlreadyOccupied check), while re-equipping the SAME item into the SAME slot is idempotent.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `actor_entity_key` | yes | string |  | actor_equipment_slots.actor_entity_key — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); place it first via spellkave_place_actor. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `item_entity_key` | yes | string |  | actor_equipment_slots.item_key — an already-authored entities row that entity_containment already places inside actor_entity_key (stow it first via spellkave_stow_item). |
| `slot_id` | yes | string |  | actor_equipment_slots.slot_id — must already resolve to an authored equipment_slot_definitions row. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "actor_entity_key": "aoe_blast/caster_1",
  "item_entity_key": "aoe_blast/lever_1",
  "slot_id": "core/slot/main_hand"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 1,
  "diagnostics": [],
  "actor_entity_key": "aoe_blast/caster_1",
  "item_entity_key": "aoe_blast/lever_1",
  "slot_id": "core/slot/main_hand"
}
```

## `spellkave_stow_item`

**Stow Item (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

sk-9ll.3: place an already-authored entity inside a container (entity_containment, upsert-by-entity_key — a re-authored containment MOVES the entity, mirroring add-entity-containment's own upsert semantics). Folds the 'starter pack straight into the hero' / 'item straight onto its holder' idiom (container_entity_key omitted, defaults to actor_entity_key) AND the nested-container idiom (container_entity_key explicit, e.g. a torch into an already-stowed field kit) into one checked call, replacing a raw spellkave_write_rows entity_containment call.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `actor_entity_key` | no | string |  | The actor stowing item_entity_key — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); place it first via spellkave_place_actor. Also the DEFAULT container when container_entity_key is omitted. Omit it to put an item into a placed container with no actor involved (a potion in a chest): then container_entity_key is required. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `container_entity_key` | no | string |  | entity_containment.container_entity_key. Default actor_entity_key — the common 'give the actor this item directly' case (a starter weapon straight into the hero's inventory). Pass a DIFFERENT already-placed container (e.g. a field kit already stowed on the actor) to nest item_entity_key inside IT instead (the torch-inside-the-field-kit idiom). |
| `direction` | no | string |  | entity_containment.direction — machine-port direction ('in'/'out'). Default '' (loose carriage). |
| `item_entity_key` | yes | string |  | entity_containment.entity_key — an already-placed entity (workspace or the active target) to move into container_entity_key (or actor_entity_key when container_entity_key is omitted). |
| `slot_id` | no | string |  | entity_containment.slot_id — machine-port slot id. Default '' (loose carriage — the common item-in-backpack/actor-holding-item case, not a machine port). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "actor_entity_key": "aoe_blast/caster_1",
  "item_entity_key": "aoe_blast/lever_1"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 1,
  "diagnostics": [],
  "item_entity_key": "aoe_blast/lever_1",
  "container_entity_key": "aoe_blast/caster_1"
}
```

## `spellkave_define_behavior`

**Define Behavior (verb PoC)** — execution mode `sequential`.

PoC : author ONE capability→affordance→action→outcome→consequence→frame_write chain (+ an optional cost debit) in a single call, granted to `grant_to`. Drives @spellkave/world-author's `clusterRows` — the SAME behavior-cluster builder the SRD content drivers use (FIX③, de-fork) — bundle-namespaced via `BehaviorConfig.idNamespace`. `primitive` fields are CLOSED PoC enums — only the real kernel shapes the worked fireball/find_familiar/core-mark examples need are wired; anything else fails loudly naming the PoC boundary. US9 VERB EXPANSION: `effect.write.primitive` now also accepts 'Spawn' (Brief 26 EffectPrimitive::Spawn — instantiate an entity_def at the actor's own node) and 'Inscribe' (the raw FrameWriteOp::Inscribe trace idiom — a durable typed footprint, no resource delta); both require `offered_when.target: 'self'|'place'` (a target concept beyond 'hit others in a radius') and never combine with `effect.shape`/`effect.per_target_gate`. `target: 'self'` needs a `cost` (else this tool errors BEFORE validation with a hint, MF-VAL-263); `target: 'place'` needs none (self_eligible stays false, so the self-budget check never engages). `effect.write.resource` (ModifyResource) / `effect.write.entity_def` (Spawn) must already be authored (this PoC never auto-creates write-target resources/blueprints — use spellkave_define_resource / spellkave_define_entity_type first); `cost.pool`, if new, IS auto-created with generic bounds. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the whole generated cluster (capability/ outcome/affordance/action/consequence/frame-write/live-wiring rows) rather than duplicating it.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `action_class` | yes | string |  | action_definition_tag applied to the generated action (e.g. 'spell'). REQUIRED — has no default (finding A1): omitting it throws a named-param error rather than silently authoring a corrupt row. Overridden (not supplemented) by `tags` when that param is set. |
| `action_prefix` | no | string |  | srd-migration round: override the derived action id's prefix — the full action id is '<bundle>/<action_prefix><id>' (default 'cast_', e.g. id='fireball' -> '<bundle>/cast_fireball'). Pass '' to derive a BARE '<bundle>/<id>' action id (e.g. the Hex/Bless/Bardic-Inspiration condition-modified-roll family's WRITER/CONSUMER pair, whose action ids are '<bundle>/<key>', not '<bundle>/cast_<key>') — mirrors compose.ts's BehaviorConfig.actionPrefix verbatim; outcome/affordance/success ids all derive from the SAME action id, so this affects all four. |
| `bind_to_definition` | no | string |  | An already-authored entity_definitions catalog id (workspace, live, or the active target — same 3-way resolution as the placement tools' `entity_def`) that inherits this call's capability at instance birth via entity_definition_initial_capability. This PoC does not auto-create the definition (use spellkave_define_entity_type first). |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `capability_id` | no | string |  | verb-UX round 2: override the derived '<bundle>/spell/<id>' capability_id — e.g. for a CATALOG spell whose entity_definitions.entity_def_id already exists under a different id shape (mirrors compose.ts's ActorBehavior.capabilityId — for a catalog spell this MUST equal the catalog entity_def_id so the capability IS the catalog identity). `action_id` is never touched by this — only the capability's own id changes. |
| `communication_speech_act_id` | no | string |  | verb-UX round 4 (SPEECH-ACT lens, Searle) — when set, the generated action's outcome_templates row carries this `communication_speech_act_id`, so the affordance SURFACES as a communication speech act while r_manipulate still EXECUTES the gated consequence normally via `manipulation_action_id` (mirrors compose.ts's ActorBehavior.communicationSpeechActId — the Persuasion 'directive' worked example). Omit for the legacy default: no speech-act framing. |
| `cost` | no | object |  |  |
| `def_instance` | no | object |  |  |
| `description` | no | string |  | Sets the generated capability_definitions row's own `description` column — the capability is this behavior's natural authoring-identity anchor, so that is where the description lands (NOT the affordance/action/outcome/consequence/resource rows this verb also generates). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | verb-UX round 2: overrides the derived 'Cast <TitleCase id>' display name stamped onto every generated row that carries one (capability/action/affordance/outcome). Omit for the smart default — naive per-word title-casing mangles a multi-word id containing a preposition (e.g. 'circle_of_death' -> 'Cast Circle Of Death' instead of 'Cast Circle of Death'). |
| `effect` | yes | object |  |  |
| `emit_capability` | no | boolean |  | srd-migration round: whether this call authors a capability_definitions row for `capability_id`/the derived id. Default true. Pass false when the capability ALREADY exists (authored by ANOTHER call/fragment, e.g. a feat grant that already created it) and this call should REUSE it — `required_capability`/`actor_capabilities`/the niche all still key on `capability_id` (which then MUST be set — omitting it AND setting false derives an id no prior call could have authored), but no duplicate capability_definitions row is emitted (mirrors compose.ts's ActorBehavior.emitCapability, a required field there, made an optional smart default here since every prior verb caller wanted true). |
| `grant_to` | yes | string \\| array<string> |  | entity_key of the caster (already placed via spellkave_place_actor) granted the capability — or an ARRAY of entity_keys to grant the SAME capability to several actors in one call (finding B4: 'author once, grant twice' — e.g. two mechanically-identical monsters sharing one scimitar). The capability/action/affordance/outcome/consequence cluster is authored exactly ONCE regardless (keyed off the FIRST entry, which also becomes `defaultCaster` for any `[[actors]]`/entities the shape itself emits, e.g. Spawn's `def_instance`) — every entry gets its OWN `actor_capabilities` grant + `spatial_niche_attachments` row (attached to ITS OWN node, resolved independently per entity_key, exactly like the single-actor case). Each caster needs a nonblank place_node_id, resolved from the workspace before the active target. If a live AUTHOR cannot read the caster's placement, the call fails before writing scratch; supply its known current actor_spatial_locations workspace row. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the WHOLE grant set — an entity_key dropped from the array on a later call has its grant and attachment rows cleared, not left behind (mirrors every other satellite this verb folds). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Behavior key stem — derives capability_id '<bundle>/spell/<id>' and action_id '<bundle>/cast_<id>' (+ its outcome/affordance/consequence siblings), unless overridden by `capability_id`. |
| `observation` | no | string |  | B-9: authored PLAYER-facing prose for what a player perceives on a successful manipulate or sensing outcome — distinct from `description` above, which stays operator-only on capability_definitions. Sets the generated outcome_templates row's own `description` column (its actual authoring/read home — see outcome_template.rs's doc comment for why that table, not action_definitions/consequence_templates). May reference ONLY the frozen placeholders `{target_name}`, `{actor_name}`, `{place_name}` (resolved from data the player already sees, never a raw id) — a state-dereferencing value (HP, a resource, a condition) belongs in the DSL outcome expression, not here, and an unknown placeholder or a description over 500 chars is rejected at validation. Omit for the existing default: the tool result carries an honest `observation: null` + `observation_gap`, byte-identical to today. |
| `offered_when` | yes | object |  |  |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | verb-UX round 2: the FULL capability_definition_tag AND action_definition_tag row set — when set, REPLACES the single `action_class` tag as the authoritative list for BOTH satellites (include `action_class`'s own value in `tags` too, if wanted — it is not auto-prepended). Omit for the legacy default: `action_class` alone becomes the one action tag, no capability tags — `action_class` itself is REQUIRED either way (no default of its own, finding A1): this param only controls what ELSE joins it, never whether it is needed. |

#### `cost`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `amount` | yes | number |  | How much to debit per cast. |
| `pool` | yes | string |  | resource_definition_id debited on cast (e.g. a spell-slot pool). |

#### `def_instance`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `entity_key` | yes | string |  | The proof instance's fully-qualified entity_key, e.g. 'srd/actor/polar-bear-def'. |
| `name` | yes | string |  | entities.name / actors.name for the proof instance. |
| `node` | no | string |  | An already-authored place_node id the proof instance is placed at. Omit to default to the resolved caster node (`grant_to`'s own node) — the niche this behavior's capability attaches is already anchored there. |

#### `effect`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `per_target_gate` | no | string |  | Authored Bool DSL expression gating the write, e.g. 'd20 < 13' (a failed save) or 'd20 >= 13' (a hit). Omit for an ungated write. aoe (effect.shape set): gates the body PER SELECTED ACTOR. single-target (effect.shape omitted): gates the AFFORDANCE itself (a miss/failed-check skips the whole consequence — the attack-roll seam). ModifyResource only — MUST be omitted for 'Spawn'/'Inscribe'. |
| `primitive` | yes | "ForEachActorInRadius" |  | Closed PoC enum — only 'ForEachActorInRadius' is wired. |
| `shape` | no | object |  |  |
| `write` | yes | object |  |  |

##### `effect.shape`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | "core/area/node_ball" \\| "core/area/sphere" |  | Closed PoC enum: 'core/area/node_ball' (topological — radius = ball_radius graph-edge hops, 0 = same node) or 'core/area/sphere' (metric — radius = radius_m). Other area shapes need direct authoring. |
| `radius` | yes | number |  | node_ball: integer edge-hop radius. sphere: metric radius_m. |

##### `effect.write`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `attacks` | no | array<object> |  | One entry per sub-attack (2+ for an SRD Multiattack, but generalises to any N) — see this field's own top-level description for the full shape. |
| `branches` | no | array<object> |  | OutcomeGraph only: one entry per branch arm (2+ — see this field's own top-level description). Required, and must be non-empty, when effect.write.primitive is 'OutcomeGraph'. |
| `condition` | no | string |  | ApplyStatus/RemoveCondition only: the condition_definitions condition_definition_id landed on (ApplyStatus) or deleted from (RemoveCondition) the single TargetActor — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create the condition (use spellkave_define_condition first). |
| `content` | no | string |  | Inscribe only: the trace's `payload_json` content — a JSON-encodable string describing the mark (e.g. '{"action":"relieve"}'). |
| `delta` | no | string |  | ModifyResource only: authored Int DSL expression evaluated per target, e.g. '-d6'. aoe: applied to every selected actor. single-target: applied once, to the ONE TargetActor. Ignored (may be omitted) when `attacks` is set. |
| `entity_def` | no | string |  | Spawn only: the entity_definitions catalog id to instantiate at the actor's own node (e.g. 'srd/monster/cat', mirroring srd/cast_find_familiar) — must already resolve (workspace or live); this PoC does not auto-create the blueprint. |
| `env_state_center` | no | "actor" \\| "target" |  | EnvState only: 'actor' (default) writes the CASTER'S OWN cell (ActorSpatialRef — follows the caster, a Darkness-shaped ambient cast). 'target' anchors on the cast's TARGET cell (TargetSpatialRef) instead. |
| `env_state_id` | no | string |  | EnvState only: the spatial_state_definitions id this write flips (e.g. 'srd/darkness') — auto-created by this call as a BOOL state def with writer_policy 'world_interaction' (so the apply path may write it at cast time) and a long freshness, mirroring `cost.pool`'s auto-create; this PoC never requires it pre-authored. A separately-authored consumer affordance reads target.state(env_state_id) — this call does not author the consumer. |
| `env_state_value` | no | boolean |  | EnvState only: the bool value the marker Inscribe writes. Default true ('on'). |
| `primitive` | yes | "ModifyResource" \\| "Spawn" \\| "Inscribe" \\| "ApplyStatus" \\| "RemoveCondition" \\| "EnvState" \\| "OutcomeGraph" \\| "ScheduledZone" \\| "Clock" |  | Closed PoC enum — the REAL kernel primitive names (US9/srd-migration round, never invented; verified against world-fixtures/srd/base/summon.toml + world-fixtures/core/base/affordances.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/hold-monster.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/lesser-restoration.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/darkness.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/acid-arrow.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/moonbeam.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/death-saves.toml): 'ModifyResource' (a resource/state delta — the original fireball-wired primitive), 'Spawn' (Brief 26 EffectPrimitive::Spawn — instantiate an entity_def at the actor's own node, the find_familiar shape; requires `offered_when.target`), 'Inscribe' (the raw FrameWriteOp::Inscribe trace idiom core/mark/core/pickup/core/drop use — a durable typed footprint, NO ModifyResource delta and NO companion definition row; requires `offered_when.target`), 'ApplyStatus' (lands a condition on the single TargetActor — the B9 Hold-Person/Hold-Monster/Bless-family shape; single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'RemoveCondition' (the INVERSE — deletes a matching target_condition row, the Lesser-Restoration cleanse shape; single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'EnvState' (verb-UX round 4 — the Darkness/Silence/Fog AMBIENT-EFFECT shape, compose.ts's 'env-state': the cast's ONLY write is an Inscribe{kind:'spatial_environment_state'} bool marker on the caster's cell (or the target cell — see `env_state_center`); this call auto-creates the backing spatial_state_definitions row, mirroring `cost.pool`'s auto-create; a SEPARATELY-authored consumer affordance reads target.state(env_state_id); single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'OutcomeGraph' (verb-UX round 4 — the branch-on-outcome shape, compose.ts's 'outcome-graph': the action's outcome invokes a graph whose `branches` (see that field) each carry their OWN ModifyResource(TargetActor, srd/hp,...) consequence, selected by the first true edge guard in array order — unlike a gated single-target write, EVERY branch can apply an effect (a Melf's Acid Arrow miss still deals half damage); single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'ScheduledZone' (verb-UX round 5 — the TRUE LINGERING hazard shape, compose.ts's 'scheduled-zone' (ADR-0054): the cast's ONLY direct write is the SAME Inscribe{kind:'spatial_environment_state'} marker EnvState uses (auto-creates the backing spatial_state_definitions row, `zone_state_id`/`zone_intensity`/ `zone_visibility`/`zone_center` — see those fields); it ALSO schedules a subject-bound ScheduleAutonomyJob (`schedule` — repeats/frequency/liveness/source) that re-fires a SEPARATE, self-contained pulse consequence each round — a node-local ForEachActorInRadius (fixed radius, ball_radius 0) wrapping `effect.write.pulse`, which REUSES this same closed enum's two autonomy-clock-eligible bodies ('ModifyResource' damage/heal via `pulse.delta`, or 'ApplyStatus' condition via `pulse.condition`) rather than inventing a third write vocabulary; `effect.per_target_gate` (if set) gates the PULSE body per occupant (the save-negate seam — Stinking Cloud), not the affordance; single-target-only, no `offered_when.target`), 'Clock' (finding C2 — the SELF-TARGETED multi-ordinal clock shape, compose.ts's 'clock' (the death-saves death-and-dying pattern): unlike every OTHER primitive above (each writes a TargetActor or a radius-selected OTHER actor), a clock's every write targets the ACTING subject alone. `tallies` (see that field) — N bare ModifyResource(actor='Actor',...) ordinals, authored first, array order = ordinal order — followed by `thresholds` (see that field) — M ForEachActorInRadius(node_ball, ball_radius 0) ordinals wrapping an ApplyStatus/RemoveCondition on 'Actor', reading the tallies' just-written state; requires `offered_when.target: 'self'` (a clock is inherently self-only — there is no 'hit others' reading of it) and needs no separate `cost` (the tallies themselves satisfy MF-VAL-263's on_success ModifyResource requirement); single-target-topology-only, no `effect.shape`/`effect.per_target_gate` (each threshold carries its OWN `when` instead of one shared per-target gate — `effect.per_target_gate`, if set, becomes the AFFORDANCE's own eligibility gate instead, e.g. "actor.status('dying') == true &&...", the same seam single-target's attack-roll gate reuses)). 'Spawn'/'Inscribe' are NOT FrameWriteOp arms nestable inside a ForEachActorInRadius body — they never combine with `effect.shape`/`effect.per_target_gate` (PoC boundary: only 'ModifyResource' selects actors in a radius). 'ApplyStatus'/'RemoveCondition'/'EnvState'/'OutcomeGraph'/'ScheduledZone'/'Clock' are single-target-only too (PoC boundary: no aoe condition/env-state/outcome-graph/scheduled-zone-CAST/clock pulse is wired — the scheduled-zone shape's OWN pulse is always the fixed node_ball-0 radius, never `effect.shape`) — they never combine with `effect.shape` either ('ScheduledZone' reuses `effect.per_target_gate` for its pulse's per-occupant gate instead, 'Clock' reuses it for the affordance's eligibility gate instead, see above). |
| `pulse` | no | object |  | ScheduledZone only: the pulse's own write. Required when effect.write.primitive is 'ScheduledZone' — a zone with no pulse body would schedule a job that fires nothing. |
| `remove_source` | no | string |  | RemoveCondition only: an exact source key to match (FrameWriteOp::RemoveCondition's `source_match: Exact`). Omit for the default 'Any' — source-agnostic removal (matches ANY target_condition row for `condition`, regardless of what applied it). |
| `resource` | no | string |  | ModifyResource only: must already resolve to an authored resource_definitions row (workspace, live, or the active target) — this PoC does not auto-create write-target resources (only `cost.pool` auto-creates, see the tool description). aoe (effect.shape set): the resource every selected actor's body write targets. single-target (effect.shape omitted, verb-UX round 2): the resource the ONE TargetActor write targets — defaults to 'srd/hp'-shaped combat use but any already-authored resource/state works (e.g. a non-HP disposition state). |
| `schedule` | no | object |  | ScheduledZone only: the ADR-0054 autonomy-pulse cadence + provenance. Every field optional — omit the whole object for compose.ts's defaults (repeats 10, frequency_ms 6000, requires_subject_alive false, source 'srd/<id>'). |
| `tallies` | no | array<object> |  | Clock only: one entry per self-targeted tally ordinal, authored FIRST (array order = ordinal order, before every `thresholds` entry) — see this field's own top-level description. Required, non-empty, when effect.write.primitive is 'Clock'. |
| `thresholds` | no | array<object> |  | Clock only: one entry per self-targeted threshold ordinal, authored AFTER every `tallies` entry (array order = ordinal order) — see this field's own top-level description. Required, non-empty, when effect.write.primitive is 'Clock'. |
| `trace_kind` | no | string |  | Inscribe only: the trace's `kind` discriminant (e.g. 'puddle_mark') — an arbitrary authored string; unlike `resource`, this is NEVER ref-checked against a definitions row (core/mark's own 'scrape_marks' has none either — FrameWriteOp::Inscribe's own doc: 'a durable typed footprint without a resource delta'). |
| `zone_center` | no | "actor" \\| "target" |  | ScheduledZone only: 'actor' (default) anchors the marker AND every pulse on the CASTER'S CURRENT cell each fire (ActorSpatialRef — a mobile aura that follows the caster). 'target' anchors on the cast's TARGET cell instead (TargetSpatialRef — the captured anchor_place_node_id stays FIXED even if the caster moves; the faithful 'dropped at range' hazard every shipped scheduled-zone spell today uses — Cloudkill/Moonbeam/Stinking Cloud/the scheduled-damage-zone batch). Mirrors EnvState's `env_state_center` — same two-value anchor concept, kept as its own field because it is scoped to a different write primitive. |
| `zone_intensity` | no | number |  | ScheduledZone only: the documentary int value the marker Inscribe stamps (e.g. the spell's damage magnitude — Cloudkill's 5d8 stamps 5). Default 0. Never read by the pulse itself (the pulse's own damage/condition comes from `pulse.delta`/`pulse.condition`) — purely an observable marker value. |
| `zone_state_id` | no | string |  | ScheduledZone only: the spatial_state_definitions id the marker Inscribe (and every pulse) reads/writes (e.g. 'srd/hazard/cloudkill') — auto-created by this call as an INT state def with writer_policy 'world_interaction' and a long freshness, mirroring EnvState's `env_state_id` auto-create (and `cost.pool`'s). Required when effect.write.primitive is 'ScheduledZone'. |
| `zone_visibility` | no | string |  | ScheduledZone only: the marker Inscribe's visibility class. Default 'Public'. |

###### `effect.write.attacks[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `delta` | yes | string |  | This sub-attack's authored Int DSL expression, self-gating its OWN attack roll (e.g. 'cond(d20 >= 11, 0 - (1d8 + 5), 0)') — a miss on THIS roll must resolve to 0, not skip the whole action (unlike the single-attack affordance-gated shape). |
| `label` | no | string |  | Human tag for this sub-attack (e.g. 'Rend'), report-only. |

###### `effect.write.branches[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `delta` | yes | string |  | This branch's authored Int DSL expression — the ModifyResource delta its terminal node's consequence applies when selected (e.g. '0 - 4d4'), written against `subject`'s `resource`. |
| `guard` | yes | string |  | This branch's edge guard predicate, evaluated root→node in array order — the FIRST true guard wins (e.g. 'd20 >= 13'); the LAST branch should carry a '1 == 1' fallthrough so some branch always selects. |
| `label` | no | string |  | Human tag for this branch, report-only. |
| `node` | yes | string |  | This branch's outcome_graph node id (e.g. 'hit'/'miss'; also the outcome/consequence id stem). |
| `resource` | no | string |  | This branch's own write resource — must already resolve to an authored resource_definitions row, same rule as the top-level `resource` field. Defaults to 'srd/hp'. Omit to keep today's byte-identical shape. |
| `subject` | no | string |  | This branch's own write subject — a kernel symbolic actor ref: 'TargetActor' (default, the damage-against-target shape every prior branch authored) or 'Actor' (the CASTER, e.g. a defeat-consequence XP credit back to the attacker — playable-fighter-l1-20 D-1). Omit to keep today's byte-identical shape. |

###### `effect.write.pulse`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `condition` | no | string |  | pulse.primitive 'ApplyStatus' only: the condition_definitions id landed on every occupant whose `effect.per_target_gate` passes (e.g. 'srd/poisoned') — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create it (use spellkave_define_condition first). Required when pulse.primitive is 'ApplyStatus'. |
| `delta` | no | string |  | pulse.primitive 'ModifyResource' only: the authored Int DSL expression applied to EVERY occupant's srd/hp each pulse (e.g. 'cond(d20 >= 13, 0 - (5d8 / 2), 0 - 5d8)' for save-for-half — fold the save into the delta the same way single-target/aoe do). Required when pulse.primitive is 'ModifyResource'. |
| `primitive` | yes | "ModifyResource" \\| "ApplyStatus" |  | The scheduled pulse's OWN per-round frame_write body (wrapped in a fixed node-local ForEachActorInRadius, ball_radius 0, by clusterRows — never `effect.shape`) — REUSES this tool's two autonomy-clock-eligible write shapes rather than a new vocabulary: 'ModifyResource' (a damage/heal delta on 'srd/hp', the Cloudkill/Moonbeam/scheduled-damage-zone-batch shape) or 'ApplyStatus' (lands a condition on each occupant, the Stinking Cloud save-or-condition shape — admits ApplyStatus to the subject-bound autonomy fence). |

###### `effect.write.schedule`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `frequency_ms` | no | number |  | Fiction-millisecond period between pulses. Default 6000 (fires every round). |
| `repeats` | no | number |  | How many rounds the pulse re-fires — bounds the duration (a subject-bound actor-reaching autonomy job MUST be bounded, server fence + MF-VAL-249). Default 10 (SRD's common 'concentration up to 1 minute' → 10 one-tick rounds). |
| `requires_subject_alive` | no | boolean |  | Whether the zone dissipates if the caster's entity is removed. Default false (the zone lingers its full duration regardless — the SRD Cloudkill/Moonbeam behaviour). Set true for a concentration-style hazard that ends with its caster. |
| `source` | no | string |  | The cancel-by-source/provenance key stamped on the runtime autonomy_job — author with the {Actor}/{ResponsibleSubject}/{tick} placeholders (ADR-0055 D-3), e.g. '<bundle>/<id>/{Actor}/{tick}', so the scheduler interpolates a PER-CAST-UNIQUE job_id at cast time (two concurrent casts never collide on the autonomy_job PK). Omit for the compose.ts legacy default ('srd/<id>', UNqualified by `bundle` — pass this explicitly for any non-'srd' bundle). |

###### `effect.write.tallies[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `delta` | no | string |  | Clock only: with `predicate` set, the increment amount (default '1') — the expression becomes 'cond(<predicate>, <delta>, 0)'. With `predicate` OMITTED, this is the WHOLE raw delta_source expression verbatim (the scratch-cell-capture idiom — see `predicate`'s own doc). Required when `predicate` is omitted. |
| `predicate` | no | string |  | Clock only: an authored Bool DSL expression — when set, this ordinal's delta_source becomes 'cond(<predicate>, <delta ?? "1">, 0)', the increment-on-condition idiom every tally-split ordinal needs (e.g. "actor.stat('death_save_last_roll') >= 10" to tally a success). Omit for a raw (non-conditional) `delta` expression instead — the scratch-cell-capture idiom a clock's FIRST ordinal often needs (e.g. "d20 - actor.stat('death_save_last_roll')", a set-via-delta that lands exactly on a fresh roll). Exactly one of `predicate`/`delta` must convey the real expression: set `predicate` alone for a plain +1-on-condition tally, `delta` alone for a raw capture, or both when the increment amount is not 1. |
| `resource` | yes | string |  | Clock only: the resource_definitions id this tally ordinal's bare ModifyResource(actor='Actor',...) reads/writes — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create tally resources (use spellkave_define_resource first, same posture as effect.write.resource). |

###### `effect.write.thresholds[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `apply_status` | no | string |  | Clock only: the condition_definitions id this threshold lands on 'Actor' when `when` is true — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create it (use spellkave_define_condition first). Exactly one of `apply_status`/`remove_condition` must be set per threshold entry. |
| `remove_condition` | no | string |  | Clock only: the condition_definitions id this threshold REMOVES from 'Actor' when `when` is true (the inverse of `apply_status`) — must already resolve. Exactly one of `apply_status`/`remove_condition` must be set per threshold entry. |
| `remove_condition_source` | no | string |  | Clock + `remove_condition` only: an exact source key to match (RemoveCondition's `source_match: Exact`). Omit for the default 'Any' — source-agnostic removal. |
| `when` | yes | string |  | Clock only: this threshold ordinal's own ForEachActorInRadius(node_ball, ball_radius 0) predicate_source, evaluated against the POST-tally state (this ordinal runs after every `tallies` entry) — e.g. "actor.stat('death_save_failures') >= 3", or an OR-branched short-circuit like a nat-20 immediate-stabilize check. A bare ApplyStatus/RemoveCondition carries no delta/predicate of its own to fold a `cond(..)` into, so this wrapper's own predicate_source is the only way to gate one — safe here specifically because every `tallies` ordinal already wrote 'Actor' alone (never a co-located bystander). |

#### `offered_when`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `range_m` | no | number |  | Affordance range_m (metres, ADR-0053 metric embedding) — author via the ft feet→metric helper (e.g. ft(5) for standard 5-ft melee reach), never a raw metre literal. Omit for the default range_m=0 (touch/same-node only). |
| `reach` | yes | "same_node" |  | Closed PoC enum — only 'same_node' is wired (its own range_m default, see `range_m`). |
| `target` | no | "self" \\| "place" |  | US9 — a target concept beyond 'ForEachActorInRadius hits others in a radius'. Omit for the legacy default (`effect.write.primitive` must be 'ModifyResource', wrapped in `effect.shape`'s ForEachActorInRadius — unaffected by this param). 'self': the acting actor targets ITSELF (action_definitions.self_eligible=true, mirrors srd/cast_find_familiar's self_eligible=true) — MF-VAL-263 then requires SOME ModifyResource in the on_success chain; `effect.write.primitive: 'ModifyResource'` satisfies it on its own, but 'Spawn'/'Inscribe' need an explicit `cost` (else this tool errors BEFORE validation with a hint). 'place': the write lands at the actor's OWN place_node with NO target-actor selection and NO self-targeting at all (self_eligible stays false — MF-VAL-263 never engages, so no `cost` pool is required or accepted); only 'Spawn'/'Inscribe' support 'place' (no fixture idiom modifies a resource with neither an actor nor a self target). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "firebloom",
  "grant_to": "aoe_blast/caster_1",
  "offered_when": {
    "reach": "same_node"
  },
  "action_class": "spell",
  "effect": {
    "primitive": "ForEachActorInRadius",
    "shape": {
      "id": "core/area/node_ball",
      "radius": 0
    },
    "per_target_gate": "d20 < 13",
    "write": {
      "primitive": "ModifyResource",
      "resource": "aoe_blast/hp",
      "delta": "-d6"
    }
  },
  "description": "Firebloom: AoE blast, flat DEX save DC13 negates, 1d6 damage on a failed save."
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 10,
  "diagnostics": []
}
```

## `spellkave_define_entity_type`

**Define Entity Type (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE entity_definitions catalog blueprint (+ its entity_definition_tag/initial_state/initial_capability/initial_condition/initial_containment/initial_equipment satellites) in a single call — the 53%-of-authored-rows cluster, folding what would otherwise be a per-tag/per-seed spellkave_write_rows call each. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. This authors the CATALOG blueprint only (placement tools instantiate entities that may reference it via entity_def). workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + EVERY satellite wholesale (fewer tags/seeds on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind). initial_containment/initial_equipment are structural (each spawns a child instance), not a flat-value copy like the other three satellites — the equipment/containment graph is cycle-checked server-side (MF-VAL-314) at admission, not re-validated here.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `affordance_seed_id` | no | string |  | entity_definitions.affordance_seed_id (default ''). |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | entity_definitions.description (first-class column). PLAYER-REACHABLE: `readAuthorizedItemDetail` (@spellkave/sdk item_detail reader) falls back to this column whenever a placed instance has no per-instance `entity_description` row, so it must hold only what any observer may plausibly know on sight — never stat-block numbers, hidden mechanics, or spoilers. Stat-block/rules prose belongs in an `srd.text` `metadata_attachments` row instead, which keeps it out of description-reading tool responses — but that is not an access-control boundary today (audience enforcement doesn't exist yet, see metadata-attachments.md). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | entity_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `grants_capability_while_equipped` | no | string |  | CSV capability ids granted to the bearer while it equips an entity of this definition (default ''). |
| `grants_capability_while_present_in_location` | no | string |  | CSV capability ids granted to entities at locations where an entity of this definition is present (default ''). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local entity_def_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='item/sword' -> 'core/item/sword'). May itself contain '/' for sub-namespacing (matches the corpus convention, e.g. 'npc/caravan', 'class/barbarian'). |
| `initial_capabilities` | no | array<object> |  | entity_definition_initial_capability rows — innate capability grants. |
| `initial_conditions` | no | array<object> |  | entity_definition_initial_condition rows — conditions born active on every placed instance. |
| `initial_containment` | no | array<object> |  | entity_definition_initial_containment rows — each spawns a child instance carried loose (no equipment slot) on every placed/spawned instance. Structural, not a flat-value copy; MF-VAL-314 cycle-checked server-side at admission (not duplicated here). |
| `initial_equipment` | no | array<object> |  | entity_definition_initial_equipment rows — each spawns a child instance and equips it into the named slot on every placed/spawned instance. Structural, not a flat-value copy; MF-VAL-314 cycle-checked server-side at admission (not duplicated here). |
| `initial_states` | no | array<object> |  | entity_definition_initial_state rows — seeded onto every placed instance at admission/spawn. |
| `lineage_id` | no | string |  | entity_definitions.lineage_id (default ''). |
| `on_consume_consequence_id` | no | string |  | entity_definitions.on_consume_consequence_id (default ''). |
| `on_destroy_consequence_id` | no | string |  | entity_definitions.on_destroy_consequence_id (default ''). |
| `slot_compatibility_predicate` | no | string |  | Closed three-form slot-compatibility grammar (not spellkave-dsl); '' or 'true' means any slot, 'false' means none, slot_id == <quoted id> means only that slot. |
| `stackable` | no | boolean |  | entity_definitions.stackable — may authored instances use quantity>1 (default false). |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One entity_definition_tag row per tag. |

#### `initial_capabilities[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `capability` | yes | string |  | capability_definitions capability_id granted unconditionally to every placed instance of this entity_def (an entity_definition_initial_capability seed row). |
| `extent_kind_ref` | no | string |  | Authored extent kind for this innate grant; preserve the same paired kind/ref contract as actor_capabilities. Omit both fields for an unscoped grant. |
| `extent_ref` | no | string |  | Extent reference paired with extent_kind_ref, copied to every spawned instance's innate capability grant. |

#### `initial_conditions[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `condition` | yes | string |  | condition_definitions condition_definition_id seeded onto every placed instance of this entity_def. |
| `duration_ticks` | no | number |  | Ticks until auto-expiry; 0 or omitted = permanent (schema default 0). |

#### `initial_containment[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `contained_entity_def_id` | yes | string |  | entity_def_id of the child instance spawned and carried loose (entity_containment, slot_id = '') on every placed/spawned instance of this entity_def (an entity_definition_initial_containment seed row). Structural, not a flat-value copy: the child's OWN initial_* seeds apply to it first (recursion). The containment/equipment graph is cycle-checked server-side (MF-VAL-314) at admission. |
| `quantity` | no | number |  | Stack-vs-instance-count rule (ADR-0028 D-6): when the contained definition is stackable, ONE instance is spawned carrying this as its stack count; otherwise this many separate instances are spawned. Default 1. |

#### `initial_equipment[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `equipped_entity_def_id` | yes | string |  | entity_def_id of the child instance spawned and equipped into `slot_id` on every placed/spawned instance of this entity_def (an entity_definition_initial_equipment seed row) — a child, one slot, implicit quantity 1. The containment/equipment graph is cycle-checked server-side (MF-VAL-314) at admission, and the equipped definition's slot_compatibility_predicate is checked at commit (MF-VAL-311/-312/-313). |
| `slot_id` | yes | string |  | equipment_slot_definitions slot_id the spawned child is equipped into. |

#### `initial_states[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `state` | yes | string |  | object_state_definitions OR resource_definitions state_id (MF-VAL-253 accepts either catalog) seeded as an object_state row onto every placed instance of this entity_def. Visibility caveat: a resource-only id has no default_visibility authoring surface, so the seeded row falls back to Public — author a parallel object_state_definitions row when Local/Hidden visibility is wanted. |
| `value_bool` | no | boolean |  | Bool carrier (schema default true when neither value_int nor value_text is set). Carrier precedence at commit: value_int > value_text > value_bool. |
| `value_int` | no | number |  | Int carrier — highest commit precedence. |
| `value_text` | no | string |  | Text carrier — commit precedence between value_int and value_bool. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "npc/goblin_scout",
  "display_name": "Goblin Scout",
  "tags": [
    "npc",
    "hostile"
  ],
  "initial_capabilities": [
    {
      "capability": "core/walk"
    }
  ]
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-254",
      "severity": "fatal",
      "message": "definition-level seed references capability_definition 'core/walk', which no manifest row provides",
      "path": "entity_definition_initial_capability.capability_id",
      "param": "initial_capabilities[0].capability_id"
    },
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-297",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "entity_definition_tag row 'aoe_blast/npc/goblin_scout' has flat tag 'hostile' with no namespace segment ('.'); either adopt the dot-namespace convention or set 'allow_flat_tags = true' on bundle 'aoe_blast'",
      "path": "entity_definition_tag.tag",
      "param": "tags[0].tag"
    },
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-297",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "entity_definition_tag row 'aoe_blast/npc/goblin_scout' has flat tag 'npc' with no namespace segment ('.'); either adopt the dot-namespace convention or set 'allow_flat_tags = true' on bundle 'aoe_blast'",
      "path": "entity_definition_tag.tag",
      "param": "tags[0].tag"
    },
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-298",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "entity_definition_tag row 'aoe_blast/npc/goblin_scout' has tag 'hostile' whose namespace is not declared by bundle 'aoe_blast', any bundle in its depends_on closure, or 'core' — add a matching '[[bundle.tag_prefixes]]' entry",
      "path": "entity_definition_tag.tag",
      "param": "tags[0].tag"
    },
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-298",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "entity_definition_tag row 'aoe_blast/npc/goblin_scout' has tag 'npc' whose namespace is not declared by bundle 'aoe_blast', any bundle in its depends_on closure, or 'core' — add a matching '[[bundle.tag_prefixes]]' entry",
      "path": "entity_definition_tag.tag",
      "param": "tags[0].tag"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_define_roll_table`

**Define Roll Table (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE roll_tables row + its ordered roll_table_entries (+ roll_table_tag/roll_table_entry_tag satellites) in a single call. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + EVERY satellite wholesale (fewer/reordered entries on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row (roll_table_entries excepted — that row kind carries no bundle_id column). Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | roll_tables.description (first-class column). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | roll_tables.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `entries` | yes | array<object> |  | One row per entry, in AUTHORED order. `authored_order` (1-based) and `roll_table_entry_id` ('<roll_table_id>:<authored_order>') are BOTH derived from array position + the parent id, matching the corpus convention verbatim — never hand-specified. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local roll_table_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='d20' -> 'core/d20'). |
| `result_kind` | yes | string |  | roll_tables.result_kind — an open string (the corpus already uses more than one value, e.g. 'int', 'outcome_graph'); no closed PoC enum. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One roll_table_tag row per tag. |

#### `entries[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `result_ref` | yes | string |  | roll_table_entries.result_ref — the drawn value/reference text for this entry. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One roll_table_entry_tag row per tag, for THIS entry. |
| `weight` | no | number |  | roll_table_entries.weight (default 1). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "loot/scout_drops",
  "result_kind": "int",
  "entries": [
    {
      "result_ref": "1d4 gold",
      "weight": 3
    },
    {
      "result_ref": "a bent dagger",
      "weight": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-210",
      "severity": "fatal",
      "message": "roll_table_entry 'aoe_blast/loot/scout_drops:1' parent roll_table 'aoe_blast/loot/scout_drops' has result_kind='int' but result_ref '1d4 gold' is not parseable as i64",
      "path": "roll_table_entries.result_ref",
      "param": "entries[0].result_ref"
    },
    {
      "code": "MF-VAL-210",
      "severity": "fatal",
      "message": "roll_table_entry 'aoe_blast/loot/scout_drops:2' parent roll_table 'aoe_blast/loot/scout_drops' has result_kind='int' but result_ref 'a bent dagger' is not parseable as i64",
      "path": "roll_table_entries.result_ref",
      "param": "entries[1].result_ref"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_define_condition`

**Define Condition (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE condition_definitions row (+ condition_definition_tag satellites) in a single call, optionally ALSO authoring the condition_remove_policy_definitions/stacking_discipline_definitions vocabulary rows it references (shared cross-condition vocabulary — upserted by their OWN id, never duplicated, mirroring the server's own upsert-in-place discipline for these two kinds, ADR-0085) and any modifier_templates (+ modifier_template_tag) it needs (also upserted by their own modifier_template_id). DSL-bearing fields (gate_predicate_source, hooks[]._source, remove_predicate_source, *_outcome_source, predicate_source, modifier_expression_source) are passed through as free text verbatim — single-parse discipline is the server's job. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the condition row + its tag satellites wholesale (fewer tags on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | condition_definitions.description (first-class column). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | condition_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `gate_predicate_source` | no | string |  | DSL Bool expression gating condition-triggered modifier application (default ''). |
| `grants_capability_while_active` | no | array<string> |  | Capability ids GRANTED to the bearer while this condition is active (default []). Enforced in capability_ids_for_actor; use this rather than a status when the thing granted is an ability to act, because affordance_template.capability_id is a structural gate a status cannot reproduce. |
| `hooks` | no | array<object> |  | condition_definitions.hooks[]. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local condition_definition_id stem; full id '<bundle>/<id>'. |
| `implies` | no | array<string> |  | condition_definitions.implies — cascade edges (each id is ALSO applied when this condition is applied). |
| `modifier_template_id` | no | string |  | condition_definitions.modifier_template_id — REFERENCE an existing modifier (default ''). Omit when `modifiers` has EXACTLY one entry (auto-wired to it); REQUIRED when `modifiers` has more than one entry (which one is the FK, otherwise ambiguous). |
| `modifiers` | no | array<object> |  | modifier_templates rows (+ their modifier_template_tag satellites) authored in this call. |
| `observable` | no | boolean |  | condition_definitions.observable (default true). |
| `remove_policy` | no | object |  |  |
| `remove_time_policy` | no | string |  | condition_definitions.remove_time_policy — REFERENCE an existing policy id (default 'core/remove_policy/independent_lifetime'). Pass `remove_policy` instead to ALSO author the row. |
| `stacking` | no | object |  |  |
| `stacking_rule` | no | string |  | condition_definitions.stacking_rule — REFERENCE an existing discipline id (default 'core/stacking/single'). Pass `stacking` instead to ALSO author the row. |
| `suppresses_capability_while_active` | no | array<string> |  | Capability ids SUPPRESSED on the bearer AS AN ACTOR while this condition is active (default []). Suppression beats a grant of the same id. Applies to the bearer's own attempts to act only — it never makes the bearer an illegal TARGET, so a spell like Speak with Dead stays authorable against a corpse that cannot itself speak. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One condition_definition_tag row per tag. |

#### `hooks[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `detail_filter_source` | no | string |  | Inline-DSL Bool sub-expression gating which event instances this hook fires for. Passed through verbatim (single-parse discipline is the server's job, not this verb's). |
| `event_kind` | yes | string |  | condition_definitions.hooks[].event_kind, e.g. 'Layer2.ApplyConsequence'. |
| `expression_source` | no | string |  | Inline-DSL Int sub-expression evaluated when the hook fires. Passed through verbatim. |

#### `modifiers[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `applies_to` | yes | string |  | modifier_templates.applies_to — the composition-axis vocabulary id (an authored modifier_target_definitions row, e.g. 'ResolutionCheck'; open string). |
| `delta_kind` | no | "Advantage" \\| "Disadvantage" \\| "Plus" \\| "Times" \\| "FlatSet" \\| "Replace" |  | modifier_templates.delta_kind (default 'Plus') — the validator's OWN closed vocabulary (MF-VAL-243), not a PoC-narrower enum. |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | modifier_templates.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local modifier_templates id stem; full id '<bundle>/<id>'. |
| `modifier_expression_source` | yes | string |  | DSL expression producing the modifier's magnitude. |
| `predicate_source` | no | string |  | DSL Bool gate; '' (default) means always-active. |
| `priority` | no | number |  | modifier_templates.priority (default 0). |
| `replace_template_id` | no | string |  | Required (by the validator) when delta_kind='Replace' — the modifier_template id this one replaces. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One modifier_template_tag row per tag, for THIS modifier. |

#### `remove_policy`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `display_name` | no | string |  | condition_remove_policy_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | The FULL condition_remove_policy_definitions policy_id (cross-bundle vocabulary — e.g. 'core/remove_policy/independent_lifetime'; NOT bundle-prefixed by this verb, unlike `id`). |
| `remove_predicate_source` | yes | string |  | DSL Bool expression; the removal path evaluates this instead of branching on the policy id. |

#### `stacking`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `display_name` | no | string |  | stacking_discipline_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `expires_at_tick_outcome_source` | yes | string |  | Int-valued DSL expression; -1 means 'leave the existing expiry unchanged'. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | The FULL stacking_discipline_definitions discipline_id (cross-bundle vocabulary — e.g. 'core/stacking/single'; NOT bundle-prefixed by this verb, unlike `id`). |
| `stack_count_outcome_source` | yes | string |  | Int-valued DSL expression over the existing row state (facts: stack_count, expires_at_tick, world_tick). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "burning",
  "description": "Ongoing fire damage from a failed Firebloom save.",
  "tags": [
    "debuff",
    "damage_over_time"
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_define_niche`

**Define Niche (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE niche_definitions row (+ niche_definition_tag satellites, + spatial_niche_attachments binding it to place nodes/edges) in a single call. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. NOTE: an attachment referencing a BOOTSTRAP-seeded niche (one with no niche_definitions row of its own in any bundle, e.g. core's 'core/passable_portal') cannot be authored through THIS verb (it always emits a niche_definitions parent row) — use spellkave_write_rows for a standalone spatial_niche_attachments row in that case. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + EVERY satellite wholesale (fewer tags/attachments on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `attachments` | no | array<object> |  | spatial_niche_attachments rows binding this niche to place nodes/edges. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | yes | string |  | niche_definitions.description — REQUIRED (unlike every OTHER verb's optional `description?`): NicheDefinitionRow kept its own PRE-EXISTING required description column through the description-column decision (no `#[serde(default)]` in the schema); omitting it would author an invalid row, not merely a less-documented one. |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | niche_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local niche_id stem; full id '<bundle>/<id>'. |
| `predicate_source` | no | string |  | DSL Bool predicate (default '' = trivially-true, matches any candidate target). |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One niche_definition_tag row per tag. |

#### `attachments[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `condition_bool` | no | boolean |  | spatial_niche_attachments.condition_bool (default true). |
| `ecological_invariant` | no | boolean |  | spatial_niche_attachments.ecological_invariant (default false). |
| `edge` | no | number |  | spatial_niche_attachments.place_edge_id — a place_edge numeric id (0 is the SpacetimeDB 'every edge' wildcard convention, e.g. a global passable-portal gate). EXACTLY ONE of `node`/`edge`. |
| `node` | no | string |  | spatial_niche_attachments.place_node_id — an authored place_node id. EXACTLY ONE of `node`/`edge` must be set per attachment (the two authored attachment shapes the corpus actually uses). |
| `visibility` | no | string |  | spatial_niche_attachments.visibility (default 'Public'). |

```json
  "attachments": [

    }

}
```

## `spellkave_define_affordance`

**Define Affordance (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

verb-UX round 6: author ONE niche-triggered ENVIRONMENTAL affordance — an outcome_templates row + an affordance_templates row referencing an ALREADY-authored `niche_id`/`capability_id` — in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds a capability to a `grant_to` caster). The US5-7 live-dungeon pressure-plate trap shape: 'any actor holding an existing capability (e.g. core/walk) that steps onto an existing niche triggers this'. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES both rows wholesale.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `capability_id` | yes | string |  | affordance_templates.capability_id — an ALREADY-authored capability_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target, e.g. 'core/walk') this call never creates — the pre-existing capability any qualifying actor already holds (no NEW grant is authored by this call). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | Overrides the derived title-cased `id` for BOTH the outcome and affordance rows. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local affordance key stem — derives template_id '<bundle>/<id>/affordance' and outcome_template_id '<bundle>/<id>/outcome'. |
| `manipulation_action_id` | no | string |  | outcome_templates.manipulation_action_id — executes a pre-authored action_definitions row instead (the darkness-consumer idiom, packages/spellkave-srd/src/author/author-darkness.ts's `act_in_dark`). Exactly ONE of `outcome_expression_source`/`manipulation_action_id` is required. |
| `niche_id` | yes | string |  | affordance_templates.niche_id — an ALREADY-authored niche_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target, e.g. via spellkave_define_niche) this call never creates — the trigger surface (a trap/trigger niche, e.g. a pressure plate). |
| `outcome_expression_source` | no | string |  | outcome_templates.outcome_expression_source — invokes a pre-authored effect (e.g. "invoke_outcome_graph('<bundle>/<id>/graph')"). Exactly ONE of `outcome_expression_source`/`manipulation_action_id` is required — an affordance with neither would trigger nothing. |
| `predicate_source` | no | string |  | affordance_templates.predicate_source — the deterministic ELIGIBILITY gate for whether this affordance offers (e.g. a capability/state check like 'target.stat("srd/ac") >= 1'). A stochastic comparison here (e.g. 'd20 >= 13') is treated as satisfied at materialise time and never gates offer — author dice on the action's resolution_predicate_source (resolution_mode = 'Stochastic') instead. Omit for an ungated trigger (predicate_bool = true). |
| `range_m` | no | number |  | affordance_templates.range_m (ADR-0053 metric embedding). Default 0. |

### Example

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "trap/plate",
  "niche_id": "aoe_blast/trap/plate",
  "capability_id": "aoe_blast/trigger/plate",
  "manipulation_action_id": "aoe_blast/cast_firebloom"
}
```

## `spellkave_define_capability`

**Define Capability (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE capability_definitions row (+ capability_definition_tag satellites) in a single call — the verb-UX round's named missing bare-vocabulary verb. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. capability_definitions is referenced from MANY affordance_templates/action_definitions rows (not satellite-owned by a single parent) — those stay on spellkave_write_rows/spellkave_define_behavior, whichever fits the calling context. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + its tag satellite wholesale (fewer tags on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `actor_kind` | yes | string |  | capability_definitions.actor_kind — an open string (the corpus already uses more than one value, e.g. 'entity', 'operator'); no closed PoC enum. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `default_visibility` | no | string |  | capability_definitions.default_visibility — the ADR-0120 read-visibility default concrete grants inherit unless overridden. Omit to default 'Public' (smart default — matches the schema's own `default_public` serde default). |
| `description` | yes | string |  | capability_definitions.description — REQUIRED (unlike every OTHER verb's optional `description?`): CapabilityDefinitionRow kept its own PRE-EXISTING required description column through the description-column decision (no `#[serde(default)]` in the schema); omitting it would author an invalid row, not merely a less-documented one (same carve-out as spellkave_define_niche's own required `description`). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | capability_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local capability_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='walk' -> 'core/walk'). A handful of corpus capability ids are DELIBERATELY cross-namespace (e.g. 'frontier.apply_manifest' under bundle_id='core') — this verb always derives '<bundle>/<id>', so a cross-namespace id stays on spellkave_write_rows (mirrors spellkave_define_entity_type's own cross-namespace carve-out). |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One capability_definition_tag row per tag. |

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "trigger/plate",
  "actor_kind": "entity",

  "tags": [
    "trigger"
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_define_consequence`

**Define Consequence (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE consequence_templates row (+ its consequence_frame_writes satellites, in authored order) in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds its generated consequence to a `grant_to` caster's action cluster). Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + every consequence_frame_writes row wholesale (fewer frame_writes on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the consequence_templates row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | consequence_templates.description (first-class column). |
| `effect_ref` | no | string |  | consequence_templates.effect_refs_csv — an already-authored effect_definitions id this consequence invokes (e.g. a scheduled-zone/summon effect). The corpus never joins more than one id here despite the column's '_csv' name — a single ref, not a real CSV list. Omit for a consequence with no effect_definitions reference. |
| `frame_writes` | no | array<object \\| "BreakPlaceSeal"> |  | consequence_frame_writes rows, in AUTHORED order — each a raw FrameWriteOp body object or the unit string BreakPlaceSeal (e.g. {Inscribe: {...}}, {ModifyResource: {...}}, {PickupTargetItem: {...}}), mirroring spellkave_write_rows' own untyped row shape (the closed Rust FrameWriteOp enum is never modeled in TypeBox here). `ordinal` (0-based) is derived from array position — never hand-specified. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local consequence_template_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='pickup/success' -> 'core/pickup/success'). |

## `spellkave_define_action`

**Define Action (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE action_definitions row (+ action_definition_tag satellites) in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds its generated action to a `grant_to` caster). `required_capability` must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target) — this verb never auto-creates it (use spellkave_define_capability first). Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + its tag satellite wholesale.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the action_definitions row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `cost_time_ms` | no | number |  | action_definitions.cost_time_ms in fiction milliseconds. With spends_channel, omit or set 0 to spend one full channel pool; without a channel, 0 is unmetered. |
| `description` | no | string |  | action_definitions.description (first-class column). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | action_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (smart default). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local action_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='pickup' -> 'core/pickup'). |
| `non_steering` | no | boolean |  | Explicit author assertion that target effects are cooperative/non-steering and need no target claim. Omit/false for conservative automatic classification; marking a hostile effect true is a content bug. |
| `on_failure` | no | string |  | action_definitions.on_failure — the consequence_templates id applied on failure. Omit for none (schema default: empty string). |
| `on_success` | yes | string |  | action_definitions.on_success — the consequence_templates id (e.g. via spellkave_define_consequence) applied when this action resolves successfully. |
| `reaction_eligibility` | no | string |  | action_definitions.reaction_eligibility — a DSL predicate over a candidate reactor (§8.4 WHO axis). Omit for not-a-reaction-candidate (schema default: absent). |
| `reaction_trigger` | no | string |  | action_definitions.reaction_trigger — a DSL predicate over the triggering event (§8.4 WHAT axis). Omit to provoke on every co-located trigger (schema default: absent). |
| `reaction_window_ms` | no | number |  | action_definitions.reaction_window_ms. Omit for an implementation default when `reaction_eligibility` is set. |
| `required_capability` | yes | string |  | action_definitions.required_capability — an ALREADY-authored capability_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target, e.g. via spellkave_define_capability) this call never creates. |
| `resolution_mode` | no | "Deterministic" \\| "Stochastic" \\| "Deferred" |  | action_definitions.resolution_mode. Omit for the schema default ('Deterministic'). |
| `resolution_predicate_source` | no | string |  | action_definitions.resolution_predicate_source — authored boolean DSL for Stochastic resolution. Omit for empty (Deterministic/Deferred). |
| `resolution_scope` | no | string |  | action_definitions.resolution_scope — open authored id selecting scoped actor-side roll modifiers. Omit for no narrow scope. |
| `resumable` | no | boolean |  | action_definitions.resumable — interrupted long-running progress is credited on the next matching promotion (same actor, action, target). Omit for the schema default (false). |
| `self_eligible` | no | boolean |  | action_definitions.self_eligible. Omit for the schema default (false). |
| `self_only` | no | boolean |  | action_definitions.self_only (ADR-0075). Omit for the schema default (false). |
| `session_def_id` | no | string |  | action_definitions.session_def_id. Omit for the schema default (empty string). |
| `spends_channel` | no | string |  | action_definitions.spends_channel — an open FK into economy_channel_definitions.id (action-economy budgeting). Omit for unmetered (schema default: absent). |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One action_definition_tag row per tag. |

### Example

```json
{

  "id": "trigger_plate",
  "required_capability": "aoe_blast/trigger/plate",
```
