## `spellkave_define_session`

**Define Session (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE session_definitions row in a single call — the first-class shape for sessions: a long-running/timed solo session (smart defaults: turn_rule 'Sequential', visibility 'Public'; set round_duration_ms=6000 + a termination_pred for tick-paced expiry) or a combat encounter (point turn_scheduler_id / combat_grid_blueprint_id at already-authored rows — this verb never creates or ref-checks them; the validator's cross-row pass judges FKs at validate/apply). Busy policy (busy_allow_pred / busy_break_pred) governs what a busy participant may attempt; both absent = full block. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row wholesale.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `auto_join_on_targeting` | no | boolean |  | session_definitions.auto_join_on_targeting (ADR-0037 D-7). Omit for the schema default (false). |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the session_definitions row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `busy_allow_pred` | no | string |  | session_definitions.busy_allow_pred — actions matching this DSL predicate (attempted action tags via target.has_tag(..), id via target.text('action_id')) stay ALLOWED while a participant is busy in this session. Omit for none (with busy_break_pred also absent: full block). |
| `busy_break_pred` | no | string |  | session_definitions.busy_break_pred — actions matching this predicate ABANDON the session (abort semantics: on_failure + progress record), then proceed. Omit for none. |
| `combat_grid_blueprint_id` | no | string |  | session_definitions.combat_grid_blueprint_id — FK into an ALREADY-authored combat_grid_blueprint row (ADR-0045/0052 tactical grid). Omit for no automatic grid (schema default: empty). |
| `description` | no | string |  | session_definitions.description (first-class column). |
| `grid_edge_affordance_bindings_json` | no | string |  | session_definitions.grid_edge_affordance_bindings_json. Omit for the schema default (empty). |
| `grid_edge_affordance_template_id` | no | string |  | session_definitions.grid_edge_affordance_template_id. Omit for the schema default (empty). |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local session_def_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='long_running_action' -> 'core/long_running_action'). |
| `initial_state` | no | string |  | session_definitions.initial_state (JSON). Omit for the schema default (empty). |
| `legal_moves_csv` | no | string |  | session_definitions.legal_moves_csv — comma-separated move-template ids `r_session_move` accepts. Omit for the schema default (empty). |
| `on_terminate` | no | string |  | session_definitions.on_terminate — a consequence_templates id applied on 'completed' termination, before the originating action's own on_success (binding order). Omit for none (schema default: empty). |
| `participants_pred` | no | string |  | session_definitions.participants_pred. Omit for the schema default (empty; currently not validated at open — architecture Phase E/F). |
| `round_duration_ms` | no | number |  | session_definitions.round_duration_ms (ADR-0037 D-5). Omit for the schema default (0 = unbound). Set 6000 for a default-tick-paced session whose termination_pred should be re-evaluated every world tick (the `core/long_running_action` shape). |
| `stakes_required` | no | string |  | session_definitions.stakes_required. Omit for the schema default (empty). |
| `termination_pred` | no | string |  | session_definitions.termination_pred — DSL predicate evaluated after every turn advance; on match the session terminates 'completed'. For a time-bound session use "world.tick - session.stat('opened_at') >= session.stat('promoted_duration_ticks')". Omit for none (schema default: empty). |
| `turn_eligibility_pred` | no | string |  | session_definitions.turn_eligibility_pred (ADR-0143) — Bool DSL predicate evaluated per participant as `actor` when the turn advances; a false result skips that participant without removing it (it stays targetable and counted). Actor-subject reads only (MF-VAL-334), e.g. "actor.status('<condition_id>') == false" or a Bool macro. Omit to hand every participant the turn. |
| `turn_rule` | no | string |  | session_definitions.turn_rule. Omit for 'Sequential' (smart default — the only rule `r_session_open`/`r_advance_turn` schedule today; other values pass through verbatim). |
| `turn_scheduler_id` | no | string |  | session_definitions.turn_scheduler_id — FK into an ALREADY-authored turn_scheduler row (ADR-0037 D-3/D-4, e.g. a RolledOrder d20 initiative). Omit for the world-active scheduler (schema default: empty). |
| `visibility_policy` | no | string |  | session_definitions.visibility_policy. Omit for 'Public' (smart default). |
| `winner_predicate` | no | string |  | session_definitions.winner_predicate. Omit for the schema default (empty). |

## `spellkave_define_action_verb`

**Define Action Verb (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE action-verb chain — action_definitions + outcome_templates + affordance_templates + consequence_templates (+ optional consequence_frame_writes) — in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds its generated cluster to a `grant_to` caster). The composite fold for the action/affordance/outcome/consequence chain (executable finding): `required_capability`/`niche_id` must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target) — this verb never auto-creates either (use spellkave_define_capability first; `niche_id` needs no niche_definitions row at all for the two common synthetic-niche shapes, see this verb's own file-header note). Omit `consequence.frame_writes` entirely for MF-VAL-222's own no-op consequence shape. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES all four rows + every satellite wholesale.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `accepts_global_storm` | no | boolean |  | affordance_templates.accepts_global_storm — modder opt-in acknowledging this template's predicate classifies as Global. Default false. |
| `affordance_capability_id` | no | string |  | actor-carried-verbs D6: overrides affordance_templates.capability_id independently of action_definitions.required_capability — for the creature-carried-statblock shape, where the ACTION stays keyed on a shared discriminator (e.g. 'srd/action/attack', an initiative-watch read site) while the AFFORDANCE's actual admission gate is a per-creature capability (e.g. 'srd/creature/black-bear/action') granted only to that creature. An ALREADY-authored capability_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target) this call never creates — same existence-check posture as `required_capability` (a non-empty value is checked; '' is not). Omit for the verb's original single-id posture (default: `required_capability`'s own value). |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `communication_speech_act_id` | no | string |  | sk-9ll.6: outcome_templates.communication_speech_act_id — when set, the generated outcome surfaces as a communication speech act (mirrors spellkave_define_behavior's own identical pass-through) while r_manipulate still EXECUTES the gated consequence normally. Omit for the legacy default: no speech-act framing. |
| `composes` | no | array<string> |  | sk-9ll.6: affordance_templates.composes — child affordance_template ids this template unrolls into on a successful manipulate (the action-composition slice, `r_manipulate`'s own composition unroll). Pass-through, verbatim, in AUTHORED order. Omit for the schema default (no composition, this verb's own consequence fires alone). |
| `consequence` | no | object |  |  |
| `consequence_id_suffix` | no | string |  | sk-9ll.6: the local suffix qualifying the generated consequence_templates id (and `action_definitions.on_success`) as '<action_id>/<consequence_id_suffix>'. Omit for the legacy default 'success'. Raw write_rows chains this verb is meant to fold use several different suffixes here (e.g. 'consequence') — set this to match an existing convention instead of falling back to spellkave_write_rows. |
| `cost_time_ms` | no | number |  | action_definitions.cost_time_ms in fiction milliseconds. With spends_channel, omit or set 0 to spend one full channel pool; without a channel, 0 is unmetered. |
| `description` | no | string |  | action_definitions.description (first-class column). |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | Overrides the derived title-cased `id` for the action/outcome/affordance rows alike (mirrors spellkave_define_affordance's own shared display_name). Omit for the smart default . |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local id stem every derived id qualifies against '<bundle>/<id>': action_id itself, plus '<action_id>/outcome' (outcome_templates), '<action_id>/affordance' (affordance_templates), and '<action_id>/success' (consequence_templates, also `action_definitions.on_success`) — matches both grounding call sites' own naming convention verbatim, never a caller override. |
| `niche_id` | yes | string |  | affordance_templates.niche_id. NOT existence-checked against niche_definitions (see this verb's own file-header note) — a bare entity_definition_tag value (e.g. 'creature') or the 'capability:<capability_id>' synthetic-niche convention are both LEGAL here despite authoring no niche_definitions row of their own, but a bare entity_definition_tag with no niche_definitions row resolves to the 'place' provider's fail-closed default (requires_spatial_attachment: true) and REJECTS every dispatch with attachment_presence — an actor-carried tag has no place attachment to satisfy it. Pair the tag with an explicit spellkave_write_rows niche_definitions row (provider = 'entity') whenever the niche is entity-provided, not place-attached. An authored niche_definitions id (via spellkave_define_niche) works too. |
| `non_steering` | no | boolean |  | Explicit author assertion that target effects are cooperative/non-steering and need no target claim. Omit/false for conservative automatic classification; marking a hostile effect true is a content bug. |
| `on_failure` | no | string |  | action_definitions.on_failure — the consequence_templates id applied on failure. Omit for none (schema default: empty string) — this verb only ever AUTHORS the on_success consequence, never an on_failure one (neither grounding call site needs one; author it separately, e.g. via spellkave_define_consequence, if wanted). |
| `outcome_expression_source` | no | string |  | outcome_templates.outcome_expression_source (playable-fighter-l1-20 D-1) — e.g. "invoke_outcome_graph('<bundle>/<id>/graph')" to ALSO fire a pre-authored outcome graph, in addition to this action's own `consequence` (independent, sequential — the action runs first, followed by the expression in the same binding context). Every prior corpus example (`srd/acid_arrow`, `srd/outcome_guard_state_branch`) sets this INSTEAD of `consequence` (an empty-consequence, graph-only action) — setting BOTH on this verb's own generated outcome row is new with this field, structurally supported (no validator or runtime exclusivity found), used to bolt a defeat-consequence (e.g. an XP credit) onto an action whose own damage/ condition writes are unchanged. Omit for '' (schema default) — today's byte-identical behavior. |
| `outcome_id_suffix` | no | string |  | sk-9ll.6: the local suffix qualifying the generated outcome_templates id as '<action_id>/<outcome_id_suffix>' (also `affordance_templates.outcome_template_id`). Omit for the legacy default 'outcome'. Raw write_rows chains this verb is meant to fold use several different suffixes here (e.g. 'hit') — set this to match an existing convention instead of falling back to spellkave_write_rows. |
| `predicate_source` | no | string |  | affordance_templates.predicate_source — the deterministic ELIGIBILITY gate for whether this affordance offers. A stochastic comparison here (e.g. 'd20 >= 13') is treated as satisfied at materialise time and never gates offer — use this verb's own resolution_predicate_source (with resolution_mode = 'Stochastic') for dice instead. Omit for an ungated trigger (predicate_bool = true) — mirrors spellkave_define_affordance's identical omit-for-ungated convention. |
| `range_m` | no | number |  | affordance_templates.range_m (ADR-0053 metric embedding). Default 0. |
| `reaction_eligibility` | no | string |  | action_definitions.reaction_eligibility — a DSL predicate over a candidate reactor (§8.4 WHO axis). Omit for not-a-reaction-candidate (schema default: absent). |
| `reaction_trigger` | no | string |  | action_definitions.reaction_trigger — a DSL predicate over the triggering event (§8.4 WHAT axis). Omit to provoke on every co-located trigger (schema default: absent). |
| `reaction_window_ms` | no | number |  | action_definitions.reaction_window_ms. Omit for an implementation default when `reaction_eligibility` is set. |
| `required_capability` | no | string |  | An ALREADY-authored capability_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target, e.g. via spellkave_define_capability) this call never creates — reused for BOTH action_definitions.required_capability AND affordance_templates.capability_id (this verb's own grounding call sites always use the SAME id in both places), UNLESS `affordance_capability_id` overrides the affordance half (see that param). sk-9ll.6: omit (or pass '') for an UNGATED verb — some authored chains (e.g. an always-hit attack with no gating capability at all) need no capability row, matching the schema's own empty-string default; an empty value is never existence-checked — only a non-empty value still requires a matching capability_definitions row. |
| `resolution_mode` | no | "Deterministic" \\| "Stochastic" \\| "Deferred" |  | action_definitions.resolution_mode. Omit for the schema default ('Deterministic'). |
| `resolution_predicate_source` | no | string |  | action_definitions.resolution_predicate_source — authored boolean DSL for Stochastic resolution. Omit for empty (Deterministic/Deferred). |
| `resolution_scope` | no | string |  | action_definitions.resolution_scope — open authored id selecting scoped actor-side roll modifiers. Omit for no narrow scope. |
| `self_eligible` | no | boolean |  | action_definitions.self_eligible. Omit for the schema default (false). |
| `self_only` | no | boolean |  | action_definitions.self_only (ADR-0075). Omit for the schema default (false). |
| `session_def_id` | no | string |  | action_definitions.session_def_id. Omit for the schema default (empty string). |
| `spends_channel` | no | string |  | action_definitions.spends_channel — an open FK into economy_channel_definitions.id (action-economy budgeting). Omit for unmetered (schema default: absent). |
| `spends_channel_placement` | no | "affordance" \\| "action" \\| "both" |  | sk-9ll.6: where a set `spends_channel` value is written. Default 'both' (this verb's original mirrored behavior) — the server reads `spends_channel` off BOTH rows for DIFFERENT purposes: an on-turn action reads the resolved affordance template, while an off-turn reaction uses the originating action definition. A reaction action with no action-row spends_channel is UNMETERED (free). Pass 'affordance' to write it only on affordance_templates (a non-reaction, on-turn-only verb where the action-row copy is genuinely dead), or 'action' to write it only on action_definitions. Ignored when `spends_channel` itself is omitted. |
| `tags` | no | array<string> |  | One action_definition_tag row per tag. |

#### `consequence`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `description` | no | string |  | consequence_templates.description (first-class column). |
| `effect_ref` | no | string |  | consequence_templates.effect_refs_csv — an already-authored effect_definitions id this consequence invokes. Omit for a consequence with no effect_definitions reference (the common case for a check-shaped action). |
| `frame_writes` | no | array<object \\| "BreakPlaceSeal"> |  | consequence_frame_writes rows, in AUTHORED order — each a raw FrameWriteOp body object or the unit string BreakPlaceSeal, mirroring spellkave_define_consequence's own `frame_writes` param verbatim. Omit entirely for MF-VAL-222's own documented no-op shape: a manipulation-dispatchable action needs a non-empty `on_success`, and a consequence_templates row with NO frame_writes at all is the validator-sanctioned way to satisfy that with no actual effect (both this verb's grounding call sites use exactly this shape for most of their generated checks). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "id": "trap/plate/inspect",
  "required_capability": "aoe_blast/trigger/plate",
  "niche_id": "aoe_blast/trap/plate",
  "display_name": "Inspect Pressure Plate",
  "predicate_source": "target.state(\"aoe_blast/plate_disarmed\") == false"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "rows_added": 4,
  "diagnostics": [
```

## `spellkave_define_bundle`

**Define Bundle (deliberate [[bundles]] header)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author (or upsert) the workspace's own `[[bundles]]` header row DELIBERATELY — the first-class alternative to every other write verb's silent `depends_on: ["core"]` auto-scaffold, named by srd-cc executable finding (ledger/findings.md). `depends_on` is REQUIRED and explicit (pass [] for a foundational bundle) — there is no default, unlike the casual auto-scaffold. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME `bundle_id` REPLACES the header row (changed params land; an unchanged re-run is a no-op). Does NOT touch `context.defaultBundle` — combine this verb with a host-side `context.defaultBundle` set to the same id so later calls omit `bundle`. The generic spellkave_write_rows escape hatch (kind: "bundles") remains available for raw row access.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `author` | no | string |  | bundles.author (default 'spellkave-verb-tools'). |
| `bundle_id` | yes | string |  | bundles.bundle_id — the bundle's own id (e.g. 'srd', 'core'). This verb authors the [[bundles]] header row itself, so there is no separate `bundle` scoping param the way other define_* verbs have: the row being defined IS the bundle. |
| `default_extent_params_json` | no | string |  | bundles.default_extent_params_json — the params_json paired with default_extent_shape_id (e.g. '{"extent_m": 9}' for core/area/cube). Only meaningful alongside default_extent_shape_id. |
| `default_extent_shape_id` | no | string |  | bundles.default_extent_shape_id (place-node-extent D-2): the shape a place_node in this bundle resolves its extent from when it authors none of its own (an area_shape_definition.shape_id reference, e.g. 'core/area/cube'). Omit to leave the bundle without a default — every place_node then MUST author its own explicit extent or fail admission. |
| `depends_on` | yes | array<string> |  | bundles.depends_on — REQUIRED and explicit on purpose (srd-cc executable finding): deliberateness is the whole point of this verb over the auto-scaffold every other write verb falls back to (which silently defaults to ['core']). Pass [] for a foundational, drop-in-identity bundle (mirroring core's own depends_on = []), or the real dependency list otherwise. |
| `description` | no | string |  | Sets the generated bundles row's own `description` column. |
| `display_name` | no | string |  | bundles.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `bundle_id` (smart default). |
| `version` | no | string |  | bundles.version (default '1.0.0'). |

## `spellkave_define_trace_kind`

**Define Trace Kind (verb)** — execution mode `sequential`.

Author ONE trace_kind_definitions row (+ optional place_node_traces satellites placing that kind at already-authored place nodes as standing, ambient traces) in a single call. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the parent row + every `places[]` satellite wholesale (fewer places on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind). Both `node_id` and `trace_kind_id` are validated at commit (sk-9ll.8): an unknown place_node or an unregistered trace kind now fails the commit instead of silently defaulting.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default). |
| `description` | no | string |  | trace_kind_definitions.description — human-readable, for authors and operator tooling. Default ''. |
| `id` | yes | string |  | Local trace-kind id stem; full id '<bundle>/<id>'. |
| `location_kinds` | no | string |  | trace_kind_definitions.location_kinds — comma-joined registered scopes this kind can attach to (e.g. "place_node", or "place_node,location_definition"). Default 'place_node' — the scope every corpus trace kind uses today, and the only scope `places[]` (below) can target. |
| `perceptible_for_ticks` | no | number |  | trace_kind_definitions.perceptible_for_ticks — how many ticks after inscription this kind stays admissible to an ARRIVING observer (ADR-0040 seam B). Omit for unbounded (a standing mark — footprints, a slime trail, a scorch); 0 = perceptible only at the moment of inscription (an EVENT, not a mark — bead sk-n16). |
| `places` | no | array<object> |  | place_node_traces rows binding this trace kind to already-authored place nodes as a standing, ambient trace. Omit to author only the vocabulary. |
| `schema_json` | no | string |  | trace_kind_definitions.schema_json — canonical JSON schema for the trace payload (flat object mapping a required key to its type name, '?' suffix marks it optional, e.g. '{"text":"string","addressee":"integer?"}'). Default '' (no contract — most trace kinds carry no structured payload). |

#### `places[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `node` | yes | string |  | place_node_traces.node_id — an already-authored place_node id (workspace, live, or the active target) this call never creates. Rejected at commit if it does not resolve to a place_node (sk-9ll.8: no more silent fallback to bundle 'core'). |

## `spellkave_set_metadata`

**Set Metadata** — execution mode `sequential`.

Set open metadata with one flat target/key/value update or an explicit atomic updates batch. target 'manifest' replaces one root metadata key, target 'namespace' registers one namespace, and target {kind, ref} upserts one object annotation. Attachment identity follows live admission: target_kind + target_ref + namespace + bundle_id; source and payload are replaced on a repeat call. The shared validator owns namespace payload semantics and admitted target kinds.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `audience` | no | string |  | Singleton attachment form: registers an absent namespace in this atomic call; never defaults. |
| `bundle` | no | string |  | Owning bundle for namespace and attachment updates. Omit to use context.defaultBundle; manifest updates need none. |
| `description` | no | string |  | Singleton attachment form: optional description when this call registers the namespace. |
| `key` | no | string |  | Singleton form: the top-level [metadata] key, or the metadata namespace for a registration or attachment. |
| `source` | no | string |  | Attachment source for the singleton attachment form; defaults to 'manifest'. |
| `target` | no | "manifest" \\| "namespace" \\| object |  | Singleton form: 'manifest' for a top-level [metadata] key, 'namespace' to register a namespace, or {kind, ref} to attach metadata to an admitted target. Omit when passing updates[]. |
| `updates` | no | array<object \\| object \\| object> |  | Explicit atomic batch. Do not combine with singleton target/key/value fields; every update is validated before anything persists. |
| `value` | no | value |  | Singleton form: a JSON-compatible scalar, array, or object for target 'manifest'; {audience, description?} for target 'namespace'; an open metadata object for an attachment target. |

## `spellkave_write_rows`

**Write Rows (generic escape hatch)** — execution mode `sequential`.

The generic long-tail authoring verb : write one or more rows of ANY Manifest row kind not covered by the narrower verbs — kernel/substrate content (extent kinds, conditions, modifiers, niches, roll tables, action-economy scheduling, metadata namespaces,...) has no narrative-authoring shape a spell/place/spawn verb was ever meant to fit. `kind` is validated against the ACTUAL schema surface at call time (never a hand-maintained list) — an unsupported kind fails loudly naming the valid set. Rows are merged into the scratch bundle and re-validated whole (merge → validate → persist-only-if-clean, the SAME safety net every other write verb uses) — never a partial/poisoned write. workspace idempotency: when `kind` has its OWN single-column natural key (`ROW_KIND_NATURAL_KEY` — the same table `commit.rs`'s ADR-0085 upsert/collision discipline is keyed against, e.g. entity_def_id/action_id/capability_id/roll_table_id/...), a row whose key already exists in the workspace REPLACES it instead of duplicating (closing MF-VAL-272 on a re-run). ADR-0146 (sk-jay0.7.174.30) extended the same upsert discipline to kinds with a WIDER ordered composite identity (`ROW_KIND_STORAGE_KEY` — junction/satellite rows such as `*_tag`, `entity_definition_initial_*`, `roll_table_entry_tag`, `spatial_niche_attachments`, `actor_capabilities`, `object_state`, `entity_containment`, `metadata_attachments`, and more): a row whose FULL key tuple already matches an existing row REPLACES it; a row that omits any of that kind's key fields can only ever append, never accidentally collide with an unrelated row that also omits the same field. The one kind absent from BOTH key tables is `consequence_frame_writes` — a Class-β 'set-level' kind (design.md D3) whose identity is the WHOLE ordered list per `template_id`, not a per-row key — so it stays APPEND-ONLY through THIS verb; author it via spellkave_define_behavior/spellkave_define_action_verb's own consequence-authoring path instead, which replaces the set wholesale. For a WHOLESALE reseed of a satellite set (not just avoiding a duplicate), the parent folding verb remains the better tool even though the composite-key upsert now prevents duplicates here too: DEFINITION-level `*_tag` (e.g. entity_definition_tag, resource_definition_tag, condition_definition_tag) via spellkave_define_entity_type/_resource/_condition/_niche/_capability's own `tags` param; INSTANCE-level entity_tag AND object_state via spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own `tags`/`resources` params (sk-9ll.7 — the parent verb here IS the placement verb, not a `define_*` verb). `turn_scheduler` and `combat_grid_blueprints` are DOCUMENTED-INTENTIONAL raw kinds (sk-9ll.4): each is a narrow one-off definition row with its own natural key (upserted here like any other kind), and spellkave_define_session's own FK columns (`turn_scheduler_id`, `combat_grid_blueprint_id`) deliberately never create or ref-check them — that verb's cross-row validation happens at validate/apply, not at authoring time — so this escape hatch is the sole author-facing path for either row kind today; no narrower verb is planned.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id stamped on the scaffolded `[[bundles]]` header (self-scaffolds if new) and defaulted onto every row that doesn't already set its own `bundle_id` (only when the target kind's schema has that column). Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (smart default) — an error names `bundle` when neither is set. |
| `kind` | yes | string |  | The exact Manifest row-kind name — a `[[kind]]` TOML table, e.g. 'extent_kind_definitions' or 'roll_table_entries'. The generic escape hatch for any row kind the other verbs (author_place/spawn/define_resource/define_behavior) don't cover — validated at call time against @spellkave/world-author's live schema surface (describeManifestSchema), never a fixed list here; an unsupported kind fails loudly naming the current valid set. See spellkave_docs (manifest-format) for the full row/field reference. |
| `rows` | yes | array<object> |  | One or more row objects in this kind's own field shape (see the manifest-format reference doc). Each row is merged as-is into the scratch bundle and re-validated with everything else already authored — nothing is persisted unless the WHOLE merged manifest is clean. |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "bundle": "aoe_blast",
  "kind": "capability_definition_tag",
  "rows": [
    {
      "capability_id": "aoe_blast/trigger/plate",
      "tag": "hazard",
      "bundle_id": "aoe_blast",
      "source": "manifest"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `spellkave_apply_manifest_delta`

**Apply Manifest Delta** — execution mode `sequential`.

Commit/flush authored rows to the ACTIVE connection-level target ('connection-level target' decision): default (no params) reads the workspace scratch and flushes it — the transaction end after write verbs (author_place/spawn/define_*). Optional `toml` is an escape hatch for an external delta string. `live` dispatches through r_apply_manifest_delta (upsert semantics, ADR-0085); `local` renders/merges into the target folder's manifest.toml. Falls back to the legacy `context.applyDelta` live port when no `target` is wired (back-compat). Requires EITHER to be wired — throws if neither is (offline authoring with no target has no flush destination). A live apply waits for a subscribed outcome: a new digest seal (ok) or a manifest_apply_outcome row (MF-APPLY code). A mid-segment commit error rolls the world back but may publish no failure row; the waiter then hits the scheduler watchdog, not a short poll. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `toml` | no | string |  | Optional escape hatch: a full manifest-delta TOML string to flush. Omit to commit the active workspace scratch (workspace.readToml) — the normal transaction end after write verbs. Pass only when applying an external/ad-hoc delta that is not the scratch pad. |

## `spellkave_export`

**Export Manifest** — execution mode `sequential`.

Reconstruct a live bundle via r_export_manifest (ADR-0086 snapshot semantics, ADR-0149 publisher only) and write TOML. The caller must be the module publisher; any other caller is refused with MF-EXPORT-001. Optional actor= keeps only that entity and what hangs off it (containment, owned_by, equipment). Requires a live connection. Pass exactly one of out= or out_dir=. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `actor` | no | string |  | entity_key of the hero to keep. When set, only that actor and what hangs off it remain. |
| `bundle` | yes | string |  | bundle_id to reconstruct via r_export_manifest (ADR-0086). |
| `out` | no | string |  | Write the rendered TOML to this file path. |
| `out_dir` | no | string |  | Write <slug>.toml into this directory (slug from --actor, else the bundle id). |

### Example

_Requires an active connection — no offline example; this tool cannot be demonstrated without a live/local target wired._

## `spellkave_diff`

**Diff Manifests** — execution mode `parallel`.

Compare two manifest TOML files semantically: rows matched by natural/composite identity, line order ignored. only-left = gaps (in the reference, missing from the export); only-right = snapshot/play; changed = same key, field-level diffs. Offline. Default ignore list drops snapshot/enrichment noise (elevation_class, visibility, expires_at_tick, place_node_id on entities/locations, object_state.bundle_id, value_bool beside value_int/value_text). Repeatable --map-key from=to rewrites entity/actor key prefixes (and fields that carry them) before compare.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `ignore_fields` | no | string |  | Comma-separated extra field names to ignore on every kind (merged with the default snapshot/enrichment list). |
| `kinds` | no | string |  | Comma-separated row kinds to compare (default: every array-valued kind). |
| `left` | yes | string |  | Reference manifest TOML (only-left rows are gaps). |
| `map_key` | no | array<string> |  | Repeatable from=to key-prefix maps (sk-0m4.54). Rewrites entity/actor keys and every string field that is or embeds that key before compare, so an export keyed candidate_1 can match a reference keyed hero_1. |
| `only` | no | "gaps" \\| "snapshot" \\| "changed" |  | Restrict the report: gaps = only-left, snapshot = only-right, changed = same key with field diffs. |
| `right` | yes | string |  | Compared manifest TOML (only-right rows are snapshot/play). |

### Example

Call:

```json
{
  "left": "packages/spellkave-world-author/docs/examples/weighted-int-roll-table.toml",
  "right": "packages/spellkave-world-author/docs/examples/spatial-minimal-cell.toml",
  "only": "changed"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "kind": "manifest_diff",
  "left": "packages/spellkave-world-author/docs/examples/weighted-int-roll-table.toml",
  "right": "packages/spellkave-world-author/docs/examples/spatial-minimal-cell.toml",
  "only_left": 0,
  "only_right": 0,
  "changed": 0,
  "kinds": [],
  "gaps": [],
  "snapshot": [],
  "changes": [],
  "unkeyed_kinds": []
}
```

## `spellkave_applyset_diff`

**Diff Applyset** — execution mode `sequential`.

Compare an applyset root (its manifest.toml and includes) with what the world remembers applying from it (the applyset memory, ADR-0145), like kubectl diff. Every row is create (not applied yet), configure (applied with other content), move (same content, other file), prune (applied before, in no file now) or unchanged. Rows the world holds but this applyset never applied are left alone. Publisher export or complete caller-scoped instance projections supply live comparison. Rows whose live value differs from the files carry a drift warning (information only); incomplete, masked, unsupported or unavailable observations are explicit. With prune=true, previews world-added rows on each entity candidate; unreadable contents are refused explicitly, and entity-content inspection requires publisher closure. Sends nothing. Requires a live connection. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `dep` | no | array<string> |  | Repeatable dependency root manifests (or their directories), loaded for validation only and never sent. |
| `dir` | no | string |  | The applyset root: a directory holding manifest.toml, or the root manifest file itself. Its includes are read too; only the root's own rows are compared and sent. |
| `prune` | no | boolean |  | Preview an apply with pruning: inspect world-added rows on each removed entity, without writing. Requires publisher closure to inspect entity contents; an unreadable candidate is reported as a refusal. Off by default. |
| `source` | no | object |  |  |

#### `source`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `fragments` | yes | array<object> |  |  |
| `root_path` | yes | string |  | Stable logical relative root name recorded in applyset provenance; never a server file path. |
| `root_toml` | yes | string |  |  |

##### `source.fragments[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `path` | yes | string |  |  |
| `toml` | yes | string |  |  |

### Example

_Requires an active connection — no offline example; this tool cannot be demonstrated without a live/local target wired._

## `spellkave_applyset_apply`

**Apply Applyset** — execution mode `sequential`.

Apply an applyset root to the world like kubectl apply: compute the same difference as spellkave_applyset_diff, send only the create and configure rows (and, with prune, retractions for rows the files no longer name) in one r_apply_bundle call with the changed part lists and the memory generation it read, and wait for the seal. Refuses before sending when a changed row cannot be updated by a delta or the validator rejects the built root plus retractions. A concurrent apply (stale generation), another root path owning the name (without force) or a world without apply authority is refused by the world. Scoped ordinary writes need a fresh complete comparable observation and a known baseline, or complete authorized Bundle absence for a new row. Force overrides known conflicts only; it cannot supply missing read coverage. Scoped entity-prune and whole-world export require publisher closure. Binding-only deltas retain their separate authority lane; mixed unchecked rows refuse. Comparison remains optimistic against later world changes. Requires a live connection. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `dep` | no | array<string> |  | Repeatable dependency root manifests (or their directories), loaded for validation only and never sent. |
| `dir` | no | string |  | The applyset root: a directory holding manifest.toml, or the root manifest file itself. Its includes are read too; only the root's own rows are compared and sent. |
| `dry_run` | no | boolean |  | Compute and report the difference; send nothing (same as diff). |
| `force` | no | boolean |  | Let the files win over observed world changes, let this root take over an applyset name recorded under another root path, and retract an entity with world-added rows or unreadable prune contents. The answer reports the meanings used as a force_used list containing world_changed, root_takeover, and/or world_added_rows. |
| `prune` | no | boolean |  | Also retract rows the applyset applied before and the files no longer name. Retracting an entity covers its authored containment, state, resource bound, equipment (the wearer side), actor, position, identity, and capability rows (those kinds cannot be removed alone); tag rows stay. Pruning an equipped item together with its slot row while the wearer stays is refused. A containment row the files replace with another containment for the same contained entity needs no retraction. Retracting an entity on which the world holds rows beyond what the files put there, or any entity prune when those rows cannot be read, is refused unless --force. Off by default. |
| `source` | no | object |  |  |

#### `source`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `fragments` | yes | array<object> |  |  |
| `root_path` | yes | string |  | Stable logical relative root name recorded in applyset provenance; never a server file path. |
| `root_toml` | yes | string |  |  |

##### `source.fragments[]`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `path` | yes | string |  |  |
| `toml` | yes | string |  |  |

## `spellkave_can_i`

**Can I** — execution mode `sequential`.

Ask a running world whether one body may perform one action on one target now, and which admission check decides. Calls the world's probe. Does not evaluate a predicate, select a template, or perform the act. admitted and disclosed are reported side by side. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `action` | yes | string |  | The action id. |
| `args` | no | object |  | Literal manipulation arguments for the probe. Supply the same selected items and either fresh expected_participants or participant_context as the intended dispatch; can-i does not compose a participant context. |
| `as` | yes | string |  | The body the question is about, as its authored entity key or its entity id. |
| `expect` | no | "admitted" \\| "refused" |  | Closed-door expectation. A differing answer is a rejection. |
| `target` | yes | string \\| object |  | The target of the attempt, as an authored key, entity id, or target reference. |

## `spellkave_explain`

**Spellkave Explain** — execution mode `parallel`.

Read authored role, binding, capability or extent-kind vocabulary. Files include the workspace closure and kernel bootstrap; live reads the connected world. Role answers include merged capabilities, contributing bundles and bound-to rows. Binding answers inspect the exact binding ID, its state, scope and derived elevation; identity details are self-only unless the publisher reads them. This grants no authority.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | string |  |  |
| `kind` | yes | "verb" \\| "persona" \\| "role" \\| "binding" \\| "capability" \\| "extent-kind" \\| "place" |  |  |
| `target` | no | "files" \\| "live" |  |  |

## `spellkave_get`

**Get** — execution mode `sequential`.

Read running-world instance rows from the publisher owner cache or a separate caller-scoped reader. Scoped reads support entities, actors, actor_spatial_locations, actor_capabilities, actor_equipment_slots, entity_containment, entity_tag and object_state with binding-held Hidden/Internal read authority. Answers include caller/world source epochs and complete, masked or incomplete coverage; inaccessible keys report not_found_in_scope. Does not read files or workspace scratch. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id. Omit when the authored key is unique. |
| `fields` | no | array<string> |  | Listing columns. Omit for the compact preferred set. Key fields are always kept. Keyed get ignores this (whole row). |
| `key` | no | string |  | Key field values joined with:: in schema natural- or storage-key order. Omit to list. |
| `kind` | yes | string |  | Instance row kind: entities, actors, actor_spatial_locations, actor_capabilities, actor_equipment_slots, entity_containment, entity_tag, or object_state. |
| `limit` | no | integer |  | Listing cap (default 50). |
| `pattern` | no | string |  | Substring filter on key fields for listings. |

## `spellkave_describe`

**Describe** — execution mode `sequential`.

Read one admitted authored entity, its place or containment chain and admitted containment, ownership and equipment. Publisher closure and caller-scoped reads use separate sources. Scoped relationships require both endpoints; an outside endpoint is marked outside_scope without its identity or label. Answers carry source and coverage information. When connected, the answer includes reads_as_publisher and connected_identity. reads_as_publisher is true only after the publisher subscription applies. Caller-scoped instance reads use current role grants and report source and coverage. An unavailable reader needs an appropriate read grant or connection selection (`sk config view`). Export and entity prune require publisher closure.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | no | string |  | bundle_id when the key is not unique. |
| `key` | yes | string |  | Authored entity_key or numeric id of an authored entity. |
| `kind` | yes | string |  | Must be entities. |
| `limit` | no | integer |  | Belonging-list cap (default 50). |
